Prior update: **`ended_reason` confirmed writing in production**: closes the loop on the link-endings work recorded below, which was merged but undeployed. `check_schedule` v26, `send_message` v23 and `auto-enroll` v20 are live (deployed from the worktree at `45b4e20`) and the **17:15 UTC sweep wrote the first two real rows** — both `status='expired'`, `ended_reason='timeout'`, `ended_by` null, swept 14m47s and 14m49s after a 17:00 expiry, i.e. inside one 15-minute cron tick. `timeout` 214 → 216; 0 links stuck active past expiry; `ended_but_no_reason` still exactly 17 (the pre-existing rows the migration deliberately refused to guess at) and not growing. **A deploy lesson worth keeping**: the first attempt bumped all three versions while changing nothing, because it ran from the main checkout — 8 commits behind, still holding the old `_shared/issueLink.ts`. The tell was `ezbr_sha256` identical across the version bump; version numbers alone would have read as success. Always verify a deploy by *content* (`get_edge_function` + grep for a string only the new code has), and deploy from a tree you have just confirmed is level with `origin/main`. **`superseded` is still 0, and should be**: `check_schedule`'s step-0 sweep runs before the send pass, so in the normal daily cadence a stale link is already `expired` before the next is issued and supersession never fires — it only wins the race on a long window like the 72 h `Final Assessment`. The `revoked` → `expired` fix is therefore latent, and its silence is expected rather than suspicious. Prior update: **The ingest has a 300-second wall, and half of every run was thinking.** Module 09 was the sprint's first failure and it failed invisibly — dead at second 300, still reading `processing` an hour later, because the work runs in `waitUntil()` after the 202 response and a platform kill executes no code, so `markFailed()` never fires. Runtime is output-token-bound at ~82 tok/s across all 22 jobs, which makes 300s worth about 25,000 output tokens — and Module 07 had used **298 of its 300 seconds**, so the pilot passed by two. The measurement that decided the fix: Module 07 spent 27,020 output tokens to produce ~14,100 tokens of page content, so **roughly half of every run was thinking, not pages**. `api/ingest.js` now runs at `effort: 'medium'` rather than the `high` default, bounds every model call with a wall-clock deadline shared across the whole invocation (a JSON retry plus a refusal fallback can make four calls, and four per-call timeouts would run 960s inside a 300s function), and drops `max_tokens` 64,000 → 32,000, which at 82 tok/s had been permitting ~780s of generation. Thinking stays **on** deliberately — disabling it lets Opus 5 leak `<thinking>` tags into a response this pipeline `JSON.parse`s, which fails the parse, fires the retry and doubles the runtime. Watch the Module 09 re-run for thinner pages; `high` is one line away. Module 13 still needs splitting. A **final notice** now fires 12 h before `expires_at` regardless of cadence, exempt from the attempt caps, with copy that names the actual consequence. Which sessions get one is derived from graph position by the same predicates that decide what happens on a miss (`_shared/criticalSession.ts`), so the email can't threaten a withdrawal the code won't perform: `gate` for a fork-gating session, `terminal` for one that ends the study, `window` for an authored override with no derivable consequence — baselines excluded even when they gate a fork. Two bugs found on the way: "terminal = no outgoing edge" typed all 48 Liliana dailies terminal (block children carry no edges), and the reminder pass had never included `'unlocked'` rows, so anyone who opened a link and abandoned it partway got no reminders at all. §26a, migration `20260801_final_notice_reminder.sql`. Prior update: **PSY240 content sprint: the foundations block is closed and the first disorder chapter is in.** Module 15 finished the reference runs, then Module 07 (anxiety) ran as the pilot paper-mode chapter — 14 pages, 5 Tier A landing on their exact catalogue slugs, all triaged, and the first run to exercise the `action: update` merge path rather than only creating pages. Two findings. **The 16 topic overviews will not come out of the module sweep**: Modules 04 and 07 between them ran two whole disorder blocks in paper mode and produced zero overviews, so the foundations rule generalises exactly as predicted and all 16 move to the reference pass — the run plan table that promised an overview per chapter run has been corrected. And **rejecting a proposal leaves its page row behind**, so the two duplicates rejected on 2026-07-31 persist as empty `proposed` shells; one of them is the target of a live link from `what-is-abnormal`, which resolves, renders blue, and leads nowhere — meaning "0 red links" was certifying one link too many — both now fixed, the link retargeted through edit_page() and 20260801_reject_drops_orphan_page_shell.sql making rejection drop the shell it created, guarded so a page with a body, a shell with a rival proposal pending, and an update rejection are all kept. Next: run 6, Module 09 (OCD), paper, native. Prior update: **React Compiler evaluated end-to-end — decision: not adopting now**: `babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0` was wired into a real production build and measured twice — once on the 2026-07-19 tree, re-run against main@`c964dea` (2026-08-01). It works: 556 functions compiled, 120 non-fatal bailouts. But the costs are concrete — production build 4s → 33s (~8×, now paid in CI on every push since `ci.yml` runs the build), and total JS 1,137 → 1,308 KB gzip (+15%), working directly against the 2026-07-11 bundle-size campaign — while the benefit lands almost entirely on internal admin pages. The games, the only code where render perf could matter, are exactly where it bails: BreathGuardian 13 bailouts, BreathBeltDemo 10, PondWatch 5 — refs-in-render and try/catch, the same violations tracked as today's ~127 lint warnings. No page has a *measured* render-perf problem, so adoption would buy nothing observable. The non-obvious wiring recipe (the naive config is a silent no-op on Vite 8) is recorded in §30 Key Learnings; the eslint warn-demotions in `eslint.config.js` and their "flip back to error on adoption" note remain the adoption path. Re-evaluate only against a profiled render-perf issue, or a compiler release that handles try/catch (~51 of the 120 bailouts). The evaluation branch was discarded rather than merged. Prior update: **Link endings now record *why*, and supersession stops telling participants to call their researcher**: `participant_links.status` was answering two questions at once — what the participant should see, and why the link ended — and it answered the second not at all. `'revoked'` was written by an admin clicking Revoke, by the one-live-link supersession in `_shared/issueLink.ts`, *and* by adherence withdrawal; `'expired'` by the `check_schedule` timeout sweep and by client-side supersession. Of 15 revoked rows, 8 had a completed schedule row and 7 did not, with nothing to separate them. Migration `20260801_participant_links_ended_reason.sql` adds `ended_reason` (`timeout`/`superseded`/`admin_revoked`/`withdrawn`), `ended_at`, `ended_by`, applied and verified live; 214 `expired` rows backfilled as `timeout` (safe: the only other writer of `'expired'` was the client `issueLink`, dead with a `ReferenceError` from 2026-06-02 until 2026-07-31), and the 15 `revoked` left NULL rather than guessed. **The behavioural change that matters**: `_shared/issueLink.ts` now marks a superseded link `'expired'`, not `'revoked'`. Norm asked whether supersession isn't usually caused by a *missed* session rather than manual cancellation — it is, and that inverts the earlier read. `send_message` reuses a still-live link and only calls `issueLink` when none is live, so the link supersession closes is the previous session's, unused and inside its window: an ordinary miss. `'revoked'` shows *"This link is no longer active. Please contact your researcher"* and 403s in `sign_in_with_link`; `'expired'` gives the soft landing (*"that's completely okay… nothing to make up"*), which is the truth. In practice `check_schedule`'s step-0 sweep usually wins the race and marks it `expired` first (209 of 209 expired rows were genuine misses) — but with a 72 h window like Final Assessment the revoke wins, and that is when a participant got told to email the lab about a normal miss. The one-live-link rule is also now **per study** (`.eq('study_id', …)`): previously issuing a link in one study would kill a participant's live link in another. Blast radius was zero today (no one holds active links in 2+ studies) but 1 participant is already enrolled in two. Five call sites updated to populate the reason, including `ended_by` for the two admin revoke paths. Noted, not changed: `auto-enroll/index.ts:344` creates a link directly rather than through `issueLink`, so the one-live-link rule never applied on that legacy non-longitudinal branch. Prior update: **`NoDefaultSlider` — a slider with genuinely no starting position**: closes the limitation left open earlier the same day. A native `<input type="range">` must hold a number, so its handle always sits somewhere; the previous fix hid the *number* but the handle still rested at the midpoint, which meant a participant whose true answer was the midpoint had to move away and back (a native range fires no change event when the value is unchanged) — friction that biased against the middle value, the opposite of the anchoring it was meant to prevent. New `src/components/study/NoDefaultSlider.jsx` keeps the native input as a **transparent interaction layer** (`opacity: 0`, on top) so keyboard, drag, touch and screen-reader semantics are inherited rather than reimplemented, and draws the track/ticks/fill/handle underneath — which is what makes "no handle at all" expressible. `onPointerDown` derives the value from pointer geometry and commits directly, so every option costs exactly one gesture including the resting value. `value == null` is the sole source of truth for unanswered; the parallel `sliderTouched` map is **deleted** from `InterventionPage`, since a flag running alongside the value is precisely what drifted apart and caused the original bug. Applied to both slider paths — `InterventionPage`'s `SliderBlock` and `VasStepWrapper`'s `StudySliderBlock`, which had the same midpoint-friction limitation. **Verified in a browser**, via a throwaway Vite-served harness (`dev-preview.html` + `.jsx`, deleted after; build confirmed clean of it): unanswered renders 0 thumbs and 0 fills with `aria-valuetext` "No value chosen yet"; all six values on a 1–6 scale are reachable in one click from unanswered **including 4, the previously stuck resting value**; thumb geometry lands exactly on `trackLeft + 12 + pct × (width − 24)`; clicks far past either end clamp to min/max; off-grid `step` snaps correctly relative to `min` (1/3/5/7/9/11 on a min-1 step-2 scale — `round(v/step)*step` would have landed off-grid, so it snaps as `min + round((v−min)/step)*step`); real ArrowRight moves it and updates `aria-valuetext`; at 375 px the ticks stay evenly spaced, the hit target is 40 px tall and nothing overflows horizontally; console clean. Prior update: **Intervention sliders: an untouched handle was being saved as a real answer**: `InterventionPage`'s slider step defaulted the handle to the scale midpoint, displayed that value, left Next enabled (`'slider'` was in `ALWAYS_ENABLED`), and on save did `sliderValues[idx] ?? mid` — so a participant who never touched the control had **the midpoint written as their response**, indistinguishable from someone who chose it. All 7 live slider items across 4 modules are 1–6 scales, so the fabricated value is a **4** — on the upper half, on items like *"Rate how terrible you believe it is"*. Worst case is `reappraisal-phase2-day7`, which has a pre/post pair (*"rate how terrible"* → *"rate again"*): skipping both records 4 → 4, a clean "reappraisal changed nothing" on the module's own manipulation check. It also defeated the deliberate even-numbered scale, whose whole point is to deny a neutral option. **No data affected** — `intervention_responses` holds 0 slider rows (154 rows, all `prompt_response`), so no participant has reached those days. Fixed: `'slider'` removed from `ALWAYS_ENABLED` (it short-circuits ahead of the switch, which had silently made the new `case 'slider'` dead code — caught before it shipped), Next now gated on `sliderTouched`, the readout shows an em-dash with a dimmed track and a "Move the slider to choose a value" hint until first move, and the save writes `?? null` rather than `?? mid` so a regression records a non-response instead of inventing one. This mirrors `StudySliderBlock` in `VasStepWrapper.jsx`, which already gated Submit on `touched` and showed an em-dash — InterventionPage's slider was the inconsistent one, not a new invention. **Known limitation, deliberately not solved**: the handle still rests at the midpoint, so a participant whose true answer *is* the midpoint must move away and back (a native range input fires no change event when the value does not change). Marking touched on pointer-down would fix that but would let a stray tap record the midpoint — the exact bug just removed. A true no-initial-position slider needs a custom control; flagged for Norm rather than decided here. Not visually verified: the only render path is the admin preview at `/admin/training`, which is auth-gated. Prior update: **`static-components` fixed and promoted back to error**: the two reports were one offending definition — `Row`, declared inside `RegisteredVsActual` in `src/pages/toni-july-2026/graphics.jsx` — seen at its two call sites. Hoisted to module scope as `RegisteredVsActualRow`; it closed over nothing but its props and the module constants, so the JSX body is byte-identical and this is a pure lexical move. **Severity note, recorded because the general framing overstates this instance**: a component created during render does get a new identity each render and React remounts its subtree rather than updating it — but `Row` is purely presentational with no state, hooks, refs or effects, on a slide that renders only on navigation, so the real cost was wasted DOM churn, not lost state. Fixed because it is trivial and because it clears the rule, not because anything was broken. With the count at zero, `react-hooks/static-components` returns to its default `error` severity, joining `rules-of-hooks` and `set-state-in-render` as zero-violation guards — consistent with the policy that only currently-violated rules are demoted. Not visually verified: `/toni-july-2026` is behind `TalksRoute` (superAdmin), so the compile plus the identical JSX is the evidence. 127 problems, still **0 errors**. Prior update: **Lint reaches 0 errors and now gates CI**: the last 103 errors were not fixed, they were *reclassified* — and the distinction matters. `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7`'s `recommended` preset ships 17 rules (12 at error) where v5 shipped two; the ~94 compiler-family errors arrived from a dependency bump, not from the code getting worse. They are React Compiler **preconditions** — the compiler auto-memoizes components and must prove each is pure and idempotent, so it objects to `Date.now()` in render (`purity`), refs touched during render (`refs`), `setState` in an effect body (`set-state-in-effect`), and so on. `vite.config.js` is a bare `react()` with no `babel-plugin-react-compiler`, so none of them change runtime behaviour today. Set to `warn` in `eslint.config.js`: `refs`, `set-state-in-effect`, `immutability`, `purity`, `preserve-manual-memoization`, `static-components`, plus `react-refresh/only-export-components` (dev-only Fast Refresh concern). **Deliberately left at error**: `rules-of-hooks` and `set-state-in-render` — genuine correctness rules sitting at zero violations, so they cost nothing and guard a real footgun. Only currently-violated rules were demoted; the other ~10 compiler rules keep default error severity as free guards. Every diagnostic count is byte-identical before and after (refs 32, set-state-in-effect 32, immutability 13, purity 11, …) — nothing was hidden, only reclassified, and flipping them back if the compiler is ever adopted leaves the backlog unchanged. `--fix` cleared the 7 stale `eslint-disable` directives (with the trailing whitespace it leaves behind stripped on exactly those lines, not blanket-stripped, since ColorMax and OwlBarn have 20 and 17 pre-existing such lines). The single remaining `no-unused-vars` — `SliderBlock`'s unused `touched` — carries a targeted disable and an OPEN QUESTION comment rather than a silent deletion, because the slider showing its untouched default is an anchoring question for Norm, not a lint fix. **`npm run lint` is now a CI step** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `eslint` exits non-zero on errors only, so the 129 warnings do not fail the job — and the comment there now warns against adding `--max-warnings 0` before the backlog is actually worked through. That comment's original "~6,000 pre-existing errors" was wrong (the real figure was 246 problems / 205 errors) and is corrected in place; the argument it supported held regardless. 246 → 129 problems, 205 → **0 errors**. Prior update: **WP4 Modules 02 and 03 ingested; the duplicate-sibling fix held and a different collision replaced it**: four reference runs, zero re-titled clones — that bug is closed. What bit instead was overlap between two catalogue targets fed by one module, twice and by two different routes. Module 02's runs went out 17 seconds apart, so neither saw the other: two supporting pages were proposed twice and the two targets came back near-duplicates, `integrative-model` cut 20.4k → 2.8k afterwards. Module 03 did everything right — sequential, triaged between, extracted — and still collided, because run 1 invented a supporting page (`classification-systems`) that was a strict subset of run 2's catalogue target; archived, inbound links retargeted first since `archive_page` does not rebind. Triage-between-runs fixes duplicate proposals and does nothing for pre-emption, so the guard is vetting run 1's supporting pages against run 2's target at triage. Also established: extracted mode is 4.2× cheaper than native on prose modules with no quality cost (native stays for the disorder chapters' tables); Module 02 cannot fill `integrative-model` at all, as the textbook states no formal integrative framework, so it is now a declared gap awaiting NIMH RDoC; and the working split is Norm running ingest + triage in the portal with trims applied programmatically through `edit_page()`/`review_proposal()`, after a hand-keyed edit left deleted headings with surviving body text. 66 pages, 0 published, 177 links, 0 red. Prior update: **Tier 3 lint cleared — and two of the "unused" variables were load-bearing**: the last 31 `no-unused-vars` are down to 1, but not by deleting 31 things. **`eslint-plugin-react` is not configured, so JSX identifiers are invisible to `no-unused-vars`** — that is what the pre-existing `varsIgnorePattern: '^[A-Z_]'` was always working around, and it does not extend to *arguments*. So `Tag` in `({ tag: Tag, key, ...attrs }) => <Tag key={key} {...attrs}/>` (BaseAvatar ×3, RippleAvatar ×2) was reported despite being used; deleting it would have broken avatar species rendering. In the same shape, `key` in `descToEl({ tag, key, ...attrs })` is destructured *precisely to keep it out of* `...attrs` — removing it would write `key=` onto the SVG element. Both are rest-siblings, so the correct fix was one config option, `ignoreRestSiblings: true`, not six edits. Real removals: 3 Keynote + 1 ToniJuly2026 slide `render: (d) =>` → `() =>` (19 slides take `d`, 8 already take none, and only these 4 ignored it); EbbAndFlow's over-destructured `staircases`/`getThresholdEstimate`/`computeBreathSyncScore`/`resetBreath`; dead `resolversRef`, superseded `ghLeft`/`ghSoilY` (plus the `GH_VIS_H`/`GH_VIS_TOP` constants only they fed); dead locals in TrainingUpload, StudySessionRunner, ExperimentBuilder, VasUploadPage, SessionEntry, SessionComplete, DebriefStep. `trialCount`/`sessionScore`/`score` became `const [, setX]` — the values are read from refs by the async trial loops, and the setters are live re-render triggers, so deleting the state would have silently dropped a render. **`ScreenerPage`'s `onFail` was vestigial**: documented in its prop comment and never called — a screen-out is terminal *inside* the component, which renders its own per-outcome card (`fail_low`/`fail_high` heading, body, resources, `showContinue:false`). Removed from the component and both call sites, along with `SessionEntry`'s now-orphaned `handleScreenerFail`; the `screener_blocked` state survives because a *returning* previously-failed participant still sets it. Deliberately **not** changed: `InterventionPage`'s `SliderBlock` takes a `touched` prop and ignores it, and `sliderTouched` is read nowhere else — so the slider always displays its untouched default value. That is a instrument-design question (anchoring on a default), not a lint fix, and needs Norm's call. 167 → 137 problems, `no-unused-vars` 31 → 1, every other rule byte-identical; `no-undef` stayed at 0 throughout, which is what proves no deleted binding was still referenced. Prior update: **The PI's CV is public, and the home address came out at the source**: `public/docs/Farb_CV_2026.pdf` (26pp, revised 2026-07-31) is served as a static asset and linked as "CV (PDF)" from `pi.links` in `src/data/people.js` — one entry, which surfaces on both `/lab/people` and `/lab/about` because each renders the same `pi.links` array. **The published file is now a byte-identical copy of Norm's own**, which is worth stating because for a few hours it was not. The 27pp version first published carried a home address and home phone on page 1, so it went up redacted (PyMuPDF `apply_redactions()`, removing glyphs rather than drawing a box over still-selectable text); Norm then cut those fields from the Word source and re-exported, which is the better fix — the public PDF and his own file no longer diverge, so a future refresh cannot silently skip a transformation step. The redaction detour left one artifact worth keeping: `scripts/check-cv-public.py`, which asserts the published PDF has no home contact details, still has the institute address / office phone / lab URL, and contains no postal code or phone beyond the campus ones. Refresh procedure is now just: copy the source into `public/docs/` and run that check. It matters because the CV is maintained in Word from a template that once carried those fields, and the published PDF is search-indexable. Prior update: **One name store, and no Ripple face on `/profile`**: the rename this follows made the duplication a live hazard, so it is gone — `profiles.display_name` is now the only store anything reads, through the new `useDisplayName` hook (`useAvatarConfig`'s shape: one React Query key, so the Dashboard greeting, `Nav`'s initial, the admin sidebar and `/profile` share a cache entry and one invalidation updates all four). Server-side already read that column — `send_message` and `processAdherenceWithdrawal` address participants from it — so a reminder email and the dashboard could have greeted the same person differently the moment either store was edited. `user_metadata` stays as the **seed** it structurally has to be (signup, `create_participant`, `auto-enroll`), sitting second in the hook's fallback chain because it reads off the session with no round trip and so renders while the query is in flight; falling straight to the email local-part would flash "Hey, norman." first. Separately the **Ripple portrait is off `/profile`** (Norm: showing the Ripple's face beside your name and then explaining that the two are different people is a confusion the page created and apologised for) — and the identity card with it, since what remained was a duplicate name, a role badge the Account table already states, and that note. Verified through temporary `/dev/profile-preview` scaffolding, since reverted; the save round trip is still unclicked. See §12f. Prior update: **Ebb & Flow session aggregates are derived, not stored — and that is now stated**: Tier 3 lint triage (41 `no-unused-vars`) turned out to be 39 cosmetic residue and one thing worth knowing: `saveEbbFlowSession` in `src/lib/supabase.js` destructured `session_score` and `session_sync_mean` and wrote **neither** — not to `game_sessions`, not to `trials`, not to `profiles`. Not a forgotten line: the game genuinely computes and passes both (`EbbAndFlow.jsx:399,406`) and **no column exists anywhere to receive them** (`game_sessions` has no metric columns; `profiles.ebb_flow_*` holds only cumulative totals). Verified this is *not* data loss — `trial_sync_mean` is stored per trial and `session_sync_mean` is exactly its mean, recomputing cleanly across all 4 existing sessions with zero missing components (0.7891 / 0.6911 / 0.8501 / 0.6976); `session_score` is likewise the sum of `computeTrialScore(trial_type, correct, confidence)`, all three of which live in `trials.metrics`. Resolved by trimming the two params from the signature with a comment carrying the recompute SQL, so the code stops implying a persistence it never performed — chosen over adding denormalized columns that would duplicate derivable data. Also removed 8 provably-dead imports (`useCallback`×2, `motion`×2, `useEffect`×2, `useNavigate`, `useRef`). 177 → 167 problems, all 10 verified message-by-message with nothing else moving; app boot-checked with no console errors. Remaining Tier 3 is cosmetic and best done opportunistically — note two traps for whoever does: removing a positional param shifts arity, and `const [x, setX] = useState()` must become `const [, setX]` rather than being deleted, or a re-render trigger goes with it. Prior update: **You can rename yourself on `/profile`, and the greeting follows**: Norm asked why the dashboard still said "Hey, Normega" when his Ripple was now called Barnes — two different names, both correct, but only the Ripple's could be edited. Your own name turns out to live in **two** stores: `auth.users` metadata (read by the dashboard greeting and the `Nav` initial) and `profiles.display_name` (read by `/profile` and every admin list), copied metadata → profiles by `handle_new_user` **once at signup** and never synced again. They had simply never diverged, because nothing could change either after signup. The new Rename control writes **both** — the `auth.updateUser` half emits `USER_UPDATED`, which `App.jsx` turns into a fresh `session`, so the greeting flips without a reload; writing only `profiles` would have reproduced the exact staleness that prompted the question. No migration: `profiles: own update safe` already permits it while pinning `role`/`super_admin`/`study_id`. `UPDATE` not `upsert`, because `profiles` has no INSERT policy for `authenticated` and a zero-row update reports success — so the call `.select()`s the row back to prove it landed. See §12f. Prior update: **Lint triage, and the dead "Issue link" button it surfaced**: `npm run lint` reported 246 problems (205 errors); triaging them found `src/lib/scheduleGenerator.js`'s client-side `issueLink()` had thrown `ReferenceError` since `9f91f31` (2026-06-02) — that rewrite renamed the parameter to `scheduleRowId` but wrote the body against `schedRowId`, so the **"Issue link" button in the admin schedule view (`StudyDetail.jsx`) has been dead for ~2 months**, surfacing the error into `actionError`. Renaming alone was not enough: the schedule table embeds `participant_links!link_id`, and this function never set `participant_schedule.link_id`, so a rename-only fix would have created the link and flipped the row to `link_sent` while leaving the row with **no action buttons at all** and a live-but-unreachable token — verified against a DRY RUN row, where rename-only yields `canIssue=false, canRevoke=false` plus one orphaned active link. Now mirrors the Edge Function's contract (`_shared/issueLink.ts`) by back-filling `link_id`; re-verified on the same row as `canIssue=false, canRevoke=true`, then the row and all global counts restored to baseline (409 links / 387 back-filled / 17 pre-existing orphans). Note the client and Edge implementations still diverge on revoke scope (client: study-scoped → `'expired'`; Edge: participant-scoped one-live-link → `'revoked'`) — left alone deliberately, as harmonizing it is behavior change, not a lint fix. Lint config also tightened to stop reporting noise: `resources/` (zips, extracted third-party drops, briefing docs — nothing under `src/` imports it, not the Vite publicDir) is now globally ignored, `no-empty` allows the deliberate `catch (_) {}` best-effort-teardown idiom in the audio/device code, `*.config.js` gets Node globals so `vite.config.js`'s `process.env.PORT` resolves, and `caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: '^_'` covers the other half of that same idiom (the `_` binding exists precisely because it is never inspected — 11 sites, not the 2 a truncated list suggested). 246 → 177 problems, every one of the 69 accounted for by rule; the remaining 143 errors are dominated by `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7`'s React Compiler family (`refs`, `set-state-in-effect`, `purity`, `immutability`), which the build does not use — deferred, not silenced. Prior update: **WP4 content sprint begins; reference mode stops re-titling its own target**: each of Module 01's three reference runs produced its target page *and* a duplicate of that same target under a second name — `history-of-mental-illness` beside `historical-traditions` (7 sections, every one subsumed by the target's 11), `research-methods-in-psychopathology` beside `research-methods` (3 of 6). Both rejected in review; left alone this would have cost two junk proposals on every remaining foundations run. The prompt permitted extra pages for concepts the source introduces that the wiki lacks, and the model read that as licence to write the target twice; it is now forbidden explicitly, with the distinction stated by example — a supporting page must be a concept the target links *to*, not a re-titled version of it. **Module 01 is done** (one paper run, 6 supporting pages; three reference runs filling `what-is-abnormal`, `historical-traditions`, `research-methods`), and `abnormal-behavior` — the off-catalogue slug that motivated `rename_page` — was archived with all **6** inbound references retargeted, 4 of them frontmatter-only and so invisible to `wiki_links`, which is plan open question 12 biting for the first time. Live: 54 pages with bodies, 0 published, 105 links / 0 red, review queue clear. `docs/markdowns/psy240_handoff.md` rewritten against those numbers for a fresh session. Prior update: **First CI workflow, built around a `verify_jwt` assertion**: `supabase/functions/verifyJwtConfig.test.mjs` closes the one gap `config.toml` could not — a new Edge Function added without a config entry silently deploys JWT-required and breaks its caller, with a successful deploy and an ACTIVE function as the only visible evidence. Four offline checks needing no credentials (every function directory declared; every entry names a real directory, which catches a typo'd section leaving the real function defaulted; every entry states `verify_jwt` explicitly; nothing left to the CLI default), plus an opt-in fifth that compares against **deployed** state when `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is present and also flags any live function with no entry at all. The TOML parsing is deliberately strict and throws on anything it does not recognise — a lenient parser that skipped an entry would report a false PASS, the one outcome that would make the test worse than useless. **Each failure mode was verified by inducing it**: missing entry, typo'd name, empty section and non-boolean value each fail with the right message and a non-zero exit, and the restored config passes 5/5. Also added `npm test` (`node --experimental-strip-types --test` over `src/` and `supabase/`) and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the repo's first, running tests + production build on push to main and on PRs. Two findings en route: `materializeSchedule.test.mjs` had been **failing to load at all** under plain `node` because it imports a `.ts` module — hence the strip-types flag, after which it passes 8/8 — and `npm run lint` reports ~6,000 pre-existing errors, so lint is deliberately **excluded** from CI, since a workflow that is red on arrival gets ignored and that is worse than no workflow. Prior update: **Ingest moves to Claude Opus 5, with a refusal fallback** (2026-07-31): `api/ingest.js` now runs `claude-opus-5` — same $5/$25 pricing as Opus 4.8, stronger on the long-form structured generation this pipeline does. The migration itself was clean: the two Opus 5 breaking changes are thinking-on-by-default and disabled-thinking being capped at `high` effort, and this code already sets `thinking: {type: 'adaptive'}` explicitly and never disables it; no sampling parameters, no prefills. **The change worth noting is the new `FALLBACK_MODEL`.** Opus 5 runs elevated cybersecurity and bio classifiers, and a decline arrives as a normal HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: 'refusal'` — not an exception — so the existing `stop_reason` check was already the right guard. What's new is that this syllabus is unusually full of material that can false-positive: suicide and self-harm, substance use, paraphilic disorders, gender dysphoria. Rather than fail an ingest for a page the course requires, a refusal now retries once on `claude-opus-4-8`; two refusals is a real refusal. Implemented as a **client-side** retry rather than the server-side `fallbacks` parameter — that needs a beta header and SDK support that couldn't be verified from here, and a wrong guess would 400 *every* ingest instead of degrading on the rare refusal. Token counts accumulate across attempts, so a fallback job's totals mix two models' rates. §29a. Prior update: (**Field Guide: rename/archive/restore, and prompt caching investigated and declined** (2026-07-31): the first paper-mode foundations run produced `abnormal-behavior` where the catalogue says `what-is-abnormal` — good content, wrong slug, already accepted, and no way to fix it without either leaving a duplicate or burning a whole module re-read. `rename_page`, `archive_page` and `restore_page` join the audited SECURITY DEFINER write path (`wiki_pages` still has no authenticated write policies). **Rename, not delete** — deleting loses version history and provenance and turns every inbound wikilink into a pointer at nothing. Building it surfaced a real defect in the existing triggers: `wiki_pages_bind_links()` only ever *binds*, so a rename would leave `wiki_links` reporting a healthy graph while the reader showed a dead link (`link_disorder_page()` has the same gap on the catalogue pointer). Rather than change triggers other paths depend on, `rename_page` cleans up after itself and **reports what it orphaned** — renaming `abnormal-behavior` orphans 2 inbound links, which I'd assumed was zero. `archive_page` reaches a state the schema already had (`archived` is in the status CHECK and `api/ingest.js` already excludes archived pages from the model's index) but nothing could set. All branches verified in one rolled-back transaction under the instructor's JWT. **Separately, prompt caching was investigated and declined**: on Module 01's real 91,863 input tokens, three reference runs cost $1.38 uncached and $1.01 with a 1-hour cache — and it only breaks even at three-plus runs against one PDF, which only one of the four foundations modules has. A 5-minute TTL would be *worse than no caching* here, since triage sits between runs and every run would write a cache the next is too late to read. Extracted mode gets the same three runs to ~$0.38 with no code change. Recorded for later: the request already puts the PDF before the volatile wiki index, so enabling caching is a one-line `cache_control` with no prompt reordering if the economics change. Prior update: (**Dashboard re-centred on one Insights widget, and two long-standing errors in the check-in data found while building it** — §12e. `/dashboard` now leads with a tabbed widget (4 game categories × 5 time windows) instead of a wall of cards; the Emotion tab is built out over `ripple_checkins` with recency-weighted positive/negative activation, a circumplex density map, a calendar heat strip that keeps the empty days, intention follow-through, and time-of-day. The two errors, both verified against live rows rather than reasoned about: **(1)** the arousal axis was drawn upside-down in three places — `composite_y` is stored positive-is-high-arousal, but SVG y grows downward and nothing negated it, so a maximally alert check-in rendered in the corner labelled *calm* and the greeting engine told wired-up users they were running low; **(2)** `ambivalence_mag` is not ambivalence but intensity — its highest score in live data belongs to a 7-positive/3-negative check-in, i.e. someone maximally good and not tense at all — so the widget recomputes with Griffin's formula instead, clamped per row before averaging (clamping the mean instead flattens every window to 0, which the first cut did until it was run against the real series). Everything is client-side over the user's own rows: no migration, no RLS change, no view. The game cards stay below the widget for now, deliberately — they are still the only place per-game stats appear. Verified through the new `/dev/insights-preview` and a scratch run over the production series; **not yet seen on a real signed-in dashboard**. Prior update: **`/welcome` reordered Ripple-first, with the Ripple's DB write deferred until consent**: onboarding used to open on two legal panels and hold the payoff — meeting your Ripple — until the third screen, while the Welcome copy promised "in a moment you'll meet your Ripple". The order is now Welcome → 1/3 Meet your Ripple → 2/3 Data → 3/3 Demographics → Habit → Finish, so a new user names and colours a companion in the first ~30 seconds and the paperwork that follows is addressed by that Ripple. The ethics-relevant half: the Ripple step now persists **nothing** — colours and name ride in React state and are written by `persistRipple()` only after the consent upsert succeeds, so no user-generated content reaches the DB before agreement is on record. Data and Demographics must stay adjacent because `CONSENT_DOC` says "the demographic questions on the next screen". Worth knowing that ordering warmth before a consent form nudges agreement partly through investment rather than information — a mild sunk-cost effect, raised with Norm and accepted, since declining still costs the user nothing and the full doc is shown unchanged. Walked end-to-end live the same day and **proven by a before/after pair**: on the consent screen with the Ripple already named, `avatars`/`ripples` were both 0; the instant both boxes were ticked, `consents` = 2 and `avatars`/`ripples` = 1 each. **The walkthrough also caught what review did not** — `ProtectedRoute`'s `needsWelcome` guard used "has an avatar row" as its proxy for "finished onboarding", which held only while the avatar was written on the last step. Moving that write to the consent step opened an exit: agree, click any link in the header `/welcome` renders, and you are on the dashboard with demographics and reminders never collected. The guard now keys on the Ripple's name to tell a part-way user from a legacy one (§13), verified against live rows — 5 legacy users untouched, 1 mid-flow account correctly pulled back. The lesson worth keeping: **reordering a flow can invalidate a routing guard that reads flow state indirectly**, and nothing in the build or the diff will say so. After the fix the account resumed at the first unsatisfied step and completed — `onboarding_complete` true, demographics written, and `reminder_enabled` true, which only a real pass through the Habit step can produce (the column defaults to false). **Reorder fully verified end-to-end.** Prior update: **`supabase/config.toml` added so `verify_jwt` stops being a per-deploy flag**: seven of the ten Edge Functions run with `verify_jwt = false` (pg_cron, server-side callers, unauthenticated links), and without a config file the CLI defaults to `true` — so any deploy that forgot `--no-verify-jwt` silently flipped them to JWT-required and broke the caller. That very nearly happened during the same-day `radlab.zone` fallback redeploy. All ten functions are now pinned explicitly in the config, including the `true` ones, so nothing rides on the CLI default. Verified in **both** directions rather than assumed: `handle_unsubscribe` redeployed with no flag and stayed `false` (v4→v5), `handle_ripple_unsubscribe` stayed `true` (v1→v2), and a sweep of all ten shows zero mismatches against intent. Both smoke-tested — `handle_unsubscribe` returns its own `token is required` 400 unauthenticated, `handle_ripple_unsubscribe` is gateway-rejected at 401, which is exactly the pair of behaviours the two settings should produce. Side effect worth knowing: with `config.toml` present the CLI no longer falls back to `supabase/.temp/linked-project.json`, so `--project-ref` is now required — that fails loudly, unlike the flag it replaces. Prior update: **A fix applied live but left on an unmerged branch has an expiry date** (2026-07-30, learned the hard way): the consent gate for admin-generated links was fixed on 2026-07-17 — `create_anonymous_participant` stopped pre-stamping `study_enrollments.consent_date` — applied, deployed as v11, verified live, and recorded as done. It was never merged to `main`. When this session redeployed that function from `main` for the `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` decoupling, the deploy silently carried main's older body and **reverted the fix**, so admin "Generate link" participants stopped seeing the consent form. Caught only because we were triaging the branch it lived on. Proven by three enrollments in `testsona`: 12:40 `consent_date` null (v11, gate fires) → 12:57 stamped (the regression) → 22:43 null again (after merging `claude/session-link-consent-form-8a00e0` and redeploying). The wrongly-stamped test row was deleted; no real participants were affected. **Rule: merge first, deploy second. A deploy takes whatever is in the working tree, so "applied live and verified" is only durable once it is in `main` — and the same applies to migrations applied via MCP without a repo file** (that branch also carried `20260717_studies_enrolled_participant_read.sql`, whose policy had been live and undocumented for six weeks). Corollary for triage: never judge an unmerged branch by its age or its name. Prior update: (**Edge Functions redeployed to pick up the `radlab.zone` fallbacks**: five, not the four the code change touched — `ripple_reminder`, `send_message` and `send-class-verification-email` for their own source, plus `auto-enroll` and `check_schedule`, which both import the changed `_shared/processAdherenceWithdrawal.ts`. Deployed via the Supabase CLI; **`--no-verify-jwt` had to be passed explicitly** for the three `verify_jwt=false` functions, since without a `config.toml` the CLI defaults to JWT-required and would have broken the cron callers. Verified after: every version bumped by exactly one, every `verify_jwt` unchanged, and all five boot — an unauthenticated POST to `auto-enroll` returns its own `Missing required fields` 400 rather than a boot error, proving the changed shared module imports cleanly. Prior update: **Field Guide: citation assistance at upload — `api/cite.js`** (2026-07-30): the citation field is a licence-required box that the portal *cleared after every submit*, so the fifteen textbook-module uploads ahead meant retyping one 180-character string fifteen times, differing by two words — which is how a licence-required field ends up inconsistent. Now: the field survives submit; a **"reuse a citation from a previous run"** picker built from `distinct source_citation` on the course's jobs (no schema change, the data was already there); and **`POST /api/cite`**, which reads the DOI off an uploaded PDF's first three pages with `unpdf` and resolves it — `https://doi.org/{doi}` with `Accept: text/x-bibliography; style=apa` returns a *formatted* citation in one request, with Crossref as fallback and as the source of the title so the operator can check the DOI belongs to the document in front of them. Free, no key, no DB writes; auth mirrors `/api/ingest` but passes **any active enrollment**, since resolving a DOI is not privileged and from WP6 the uploader is a student. **A suggestion is never written into the field on its own** — accepting is one click but it has to be a click, because a looked-up citation carries the authority of having been looked up, so one nobody read is worse than one typed badly (Norm's call, and the reason it matters is that students will be the ones submitting). Verified against the live APIs first: five realistic DOI forms extract correctly, the textbook correctly yields *no DOI* — the path the sprint actually uses, since open-licensed books have none — and doi.org returned better citations than the hand-written ones already in the database, adding volume, issue and pages. §29a. Prior update: (**Plan: mandatory sessions + completion-anchored scheduling** (2026-07-30, nothing built): `docs/markdowns/mandatory_session_gating_plan.md`. Liliana's 3-day midpoint gap (`t_mid` offset 13 → `t_p2_*` offset 16) is a hardcoded stand-in for the 72h completion window, because every date is `addDays(t0Date, offset)` — anchored to enrollment, never to what the participant did. All four in-flight participants completed the midpoint the morning it arrived and still waited 3 days. Plan is an anchor rebase in `materializeSchedule.emit()`: when the walk passes a completed gate session the anchor becomes (completion date in lab tz, gate offset), so downstream = completion + 1 day and the whole tail shifts with it. No-op for on-time completers by construction. Norm's decisions: mandatory SESSIONS only (not blocks), midnight/calendar-date cutoff, everything downstream shifts. Rejected his initial static-worst-case-plan-plus-reschedule approach: `s_mid` points straight at a 3-arm randomize so downstream rows cannot exist before the draw, and the materializer already defers them — the deferral the approach needed is already there, making the reschedule pass unnecessary. Prior update: (**Housekeeping after the account-area rework signed off** (§12b/§12d): Norm confirmed `delete_own_account()` works — executed against a throwaway `testuser1@radlab.zone` — plus the games-page categories/buckets/numbers, the two About-page copy changes, and the reminder toggles working signed-in. Two cleanups settled. (1) **`profiles.reminder_frequency` dropped** (`20260730_drop_profiles_reminder_frequency.sql`): verified unreferenced by any function, view, materialized view or index, and by anything in the repo but prose. 182 of 184 rows held the `'none'` default; exactly two had set anything (one `weekly`, one `biweekly`) and neither ever received an email because no sender existed. Deliberately **not** migrated into `ripples.reminder_enabled` — switching on somebody's email from a preference they gave a control that visibly did nothing is the opt-in `ripple_spec` §5 exists to prevent. The `weekly` user already has real reminders on; the `biweekly` user has no `ripples` row at all and was left alone. (2) **`radlab.vercel.app` fallbacks retired** for `SITE_URL`/`FROM_EMAIL` across `ripple_reminder`, `send_message`, `send-class-verification-email`, `_shared/processAdherenceWithdrawal`, `.env.example` and `functions/README.md` — all now default to `radlab.zone`. `research@radlab.vercel.app` could never have been a verified Resend sender, so falling through to it guaranteed a silent failure. **Not redeployed**: inert while the secrets are set, so it lands at the next deploy of those four; `ripple_reminder`'s deployed source was confirmed byte-identical to the repo first, so a redeploy clobbers nothing. Prior update: **`auto-enroll` rate limiting: `enrollment_attempts` finally wired up, six weeks after it was created** (2026-07-30, at Norm's call): the table arrived with `20260617_external_enrollment.sql` — study_id, salted IP hash, timestamp, its own lookup index, RLS on with **no policies deliberately** (service-role only; the audit query can't distinguish that from the broken state, which is why it kept getting flagged). It was then never referenced by any edge function, database function or client — `git log -S` across all history returns nothing — so it held exactly one row from a manual test on 2026-06-23 while the endpoint stayed open. The exposure: `external_id` comes straight off the join URL (`PROLIFIC_PID` / `id`), so anyone holding a study link can vary it and mint a participant account, enrollment and materialized schedule per request. Repeating the *same* id was already harmless (that path returns the existing link). Bounded by one thing: synthetic `@participants.radlab.zone` addresses resolve to `null` in `resolveParticipantEmail`, so junk accounts generate **no outbound mail and no bounce damage** — the cost was polluted study data, not deliverability. Now: **new accounts only** are throttled, default 1 per IP per 60 s (`ENROLL_RATE_MAX` / `ENROLL_RATE_WINDOW_S` / `ENROLL_IP_SALT`, all optional). Re-entry with an existing id is never throttled — a participant reloading their own link must never be told to wait. Every limiter failure path is **fail-open**: a lookup error, or a request with no IP header, logs and lets the participant through, because a limiter outage must not stand between a real participant and their study. Verified live against `testsona`: 1st new id → 200 + token; 2nd new id, same IP, same second → **429**, and `auth.users` confirms **no account was created**; re-entry with the first id → 200, same token. Ledger self-prunes past 24 h. Known limits, recorded rather than solved: per-IP only, so it does nothing against distributed requests, and a shared campus or lab network looks identical to abuse — which is why the threshold is env-tunable. Prior update: (**Avatar menu items were unclickable — fixed** (§12b): the dropdown opened but every item just made it vanish. `AccountMenu` is rendered twice (desktop bar + mobile bar, one always `display:none`) and its `open` state had been lifted into `Nav` and shared, so **both** copies mounted a dropdown and **both** attached a document `mousedown` listener. Clicking an item in the visible menu fired the hidden copy's outside-click handler — its wrapper doesn't contain the visible item — closing the menu on `mousedown` and unmounting the `<Link>` before `click` could fire. State is now local per instance, so only the copy you opened exists or listens. Reproduced first (`mousedown` on an item closed the menu; two `[role="menu"]` nodes in the DOM), then verified fixed: one menu node, `mousedown` no longer closes, and all four items navigate at 1280 and 375. The earlier note calling the duplication "inert" was wrong — `display:none` hides markup, it does not stop effects or document listeners. Prior update: **Password reset never reached the reset form, and `admin_delete_user` could not delete anyone real** — two fixes, §12d and §12c. *Reset*: Supabase silently swaps in the Site URL when `redirect_to` is not allowlisted; probing `/auth/v1/verify` with a bogus token showed only `radlab.vercel.app` is allowlisted, so a reset requested from `radlab.zone`/`www`/localhost lands on the **root page** with a valid recovery hash — the user is silently signed in and never sees the password form, exactly as Norm reported. **The real fix is a dashboard change Norm must make** (add the real origins to Redirect URLs, and move Site URL off `radlab.vercel.app` onto **`https://radlab.zone`**, which is the canonical domain — `www` 308s to it and the RA-generated participant links already hardcode it); shipped here is a pre-module inline script in `index.html` that moves any stray `type=recovery` hash to `/reset-password`, deliberately ahead of the bundle because `supabase-js` strips the hash during init. *Delete*: the cascade had not moved since 2026-07-12, and every table added since — plus the whole participant tier — has a `NO ACTION` FK to `profiles`, so the RPC aborted on anyone with real data; it only ever worked on near-empty test accounts. Refreshed with 18 missing tables, participant data now deleted (a `NO ACTION` FK cannot "preserve" anything, it only fails), lab-authored content preserved with `created_by` nulled or, where `NOT NULL`, reassigned to the acting admin. Verified by two dry runs on live data inside `DO` blocks ending in `RAISE`, so nothing persisted — counts identical either side. Prior update: **Account area split four ways behind an avatar menu** (§12b): the header avatar is now a dropdown — My Ripple · Profile · Settings · Sign out — and the standalone Sign out button is gone from the bar and the mobile drawer. `/profile` had accumulated five unrelated jobs; Ripple identity and appearance moved to new **`/ripple`**, every prompt/reminder control moved to new **`/settings`**, and the Dashboard's `// Account` block moved up to `/profile`. The Dashboard's `// Reminders` block was **deleted, not migrated** — it wrote `profiles.reminder_frequency`, which nothing has ever read (the live engine reads `ripples.reminder_enabled`/`reminder_time`), so anyone who set "Weekly" there had been getting nothing. `/settings` also gains **change password**, gated behind a re-auth because Supabase's `updateUser` doesn't ask for the old one, and **delete account**, backed by a new `delete_own_account()` RPC — `SECURITY DEFINER`, keyed on `auth.uid()` with no target argument, **public tier only** (participants' rows are study data; lab members author content with `NO ACTION` FKs), delete list derived from a live FK audit and confirmed against a query showing no public profile holds a row in any table it misses. **`delete_own_account()` has never been executed** — test it on a throwaway public account first. This work also surfaced that `admin_delete_user` is stale and will now raise an FK error on participants and lab members; not fixed here. Prior update: **Games page reorganized against the revised Figma design** (node `4047:3653`, Onboarding Redesign v2 — see §12a): new `src/data/games.js` catalog is the single source of truth for all 11 games, ending the copy fork where `GamesPage.jsx` and `PlatformPage.jsx` each carried their own drifted blurbs. `GamesPage.jsx` rewritten — sort by Category (default) or Duration, live per-section counts, cards at the Figma's 480px two-up, hover-only "Play now →" layered over a card that is itself the link, locked-card veil with the padlock stacked above the unlock line. **`/games` is now public read-only**: guests browse the whole catalogue with nothing locked and no check-in card, and every card routes to `/signup`; the header's guest "Games" pill became a real link (Dashboard stays inert). **Two new unlock gates** — Face Read ← Still Water and Breath Guardian ← Contact, joining Ebb & Flow ← Contact — all three answered by one `profiles` read (`still_water_sessions`, `first_contact_complete`), since those are where the gating games record completion rather than `game_sessions`. **Daily check-in reminder** above the grid for logged-in users, mirroring `Dashboard.jsx`'s `checkedInToday` test. Duration/trials are **derived from each game's own constants, not from the mock** — the Figma's two frames disagreed with each other — and the duration buckets were re-tuned to *A minute or two / Three to five minutes / At your own pace* because the real numbers put 8 of 11 games under five minutes, which left the mock's middle bucket nearly empty. Follow-ups landed the same day: the old `EbbFlowGuard` was generalized into **`UnlockGuard`**, now on all three gated routes, so the padlock is enforced rather than cosmetic (bounce banners resolve `?from=` through the catalog, and `StillWater` gained the banner `FirstContact` already had); and **`PlatformPage.jsx`'s three-game carousel was folded onto the catalog** — its `GameCard` takes a `game` object now, with only the SVG illustration and caption still local. That fold changed two strings on the About page worth a look: "First Contact" became "Contact", and the blurb lost "Required before anything else." Guest state verified in-browser (11 cards, all → `/signup`, no console errors, 480px two-up at 1280 and single column at 375, About carousel rendering catalog values); the logged-in states were verified by temporarily forcing them to render, **not** by a real signed-in session — Norm's own login is the outstanding check. Prior update: **`ripple_reminder` test override — the email class is now observable on demand** (2026-07-30): closes the gap that let WP6 read as shipped for 16 days while delivering nothing. The email could only be seen by being a due recipient inside one of three Toronto windows, so nobody ever saw one. `POST {"test_override_email": "…"}` now bypasses the window, the cadence/staleness filter and the once-per-day dedup, and **deliberately does not write `last_reminder_sent_on`** — a test can never suppress somebody's real reminder later that day. Auth mirrors `send_message`: service key (cron/curl) **or** a lab-role caller JWT, verified with the service client rather than `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (deprecated; legacy value revoked this morning). Content is byte-identical to a real send *including a real unsubscribe token*, which is the part most worth eyeballing — so the token must belong to an actual account, hence `test_as_user_id` when the service key is used and there's no caller identity to borrow. Render+send was factored into one `deliverRippleEmail()` used by both paths, because a test that renders its own email drifts from the real one and stops being evidence; only the cron path stamps `last_reminder_sent_on`. Verified without sending: override branch reached and refused (400, exact message) when `test_as_user_id` is missing; normal path still returns `no_window_at_hour_15`; no-auth and anon-key-as-bearer both 401. Recipe (curl + a SQL form that borrows the credential from the working cron job so the key is never pasted) in `supabase/functions/README.md`. Prior update: (**`dbWrite()` — a supabase write that can't fail silently** (2026-07-30): `src/lib/dbWrite.js`, applied to the 13 highest-cost writes found by the `.update()` sweep. supabase-js never throws on a database error, it returns `{ data, error }`, so a bare `await supabase.from(…).update(…)` discards RLS denials, constraint violations and network failures identically. It catches **two** distinct failures, because today produced one of each: (1) `error` set, and (2) **zero rows affected with no error at all** — an RLS `USING` clause that doesn't match filters the row out rather than raising, so PostgREST reports success having changed nothing, which is also what `.eq()` on a missing row looks like (the `ripples` settings bug). Checking `error` alone would have caught **neither** of the morning's two bugs; detecting (2) needs `.select()` on the write plus `{ expectRows: true }`. **Never throws** — these sit in game-completion and study-flow paths, where a lost `ended_at` stamp must not become a crashed session for a participant mid-task; callers get `{ ok, data, error, reason }`. Retries once on transient failures only (network/5xx); RLS and constraint failures are deterministic and aren't retried. `onWriteFailure()` lets a UI layer subscribe later without touching call sites. Applied to: `game_sessions.ended_at` ×5 (Delve, Tune, Drift, FaceRead, BreathBelt), `liliana_day_data` ×2 (`completed_at`, `module_id`), and 6 `profiles` writes (game progress, check-in +5 points, `reminder_frequency`, Ebb & Flow mode). 12 checks in `src/lib/dbWrite.test.mjs` (`node src/lib/dbWrite.test.mjs`), including that zero-rows is not reported as an error and that a non-transient failure is not retried. **Not applied** to the remaining ~27 sites (admin config toggles, edge-function bookkeeping) where a silent failure is self-evident on reload rather than data loss. Live RLS audit run at the same time: every table behind these writes has update-capable policies today, and the only two tables with RLS enabled and zero policies — `enrollment_attempts`, `ripple_unsubscribe_tokens` — are unreachable from browser code, so this is prophylactic rather than a fix. That fold changed two strings on the About page worth a look: "First Contact" became "Contact", and the blurb lost "Required before anything else." Guest state verified in-browser (11 cards, all → `/signup`, no console errors, 480px two-up at 1280 and single column at 375, About carousel rendering catalog values); the logged-in states were verified by temporarily forcing them to render, **not** by a real signed-in session — Norm's own login is the outstanding check. Prior update: **`.update().eq(` swept for silent no-ops; one real find, fixed** (2026-07-30): follow-up to the entry below, across all **79** supabase `.update()` sites in `src/` and `supabase/functions/`. Ten are keyed on a user column (the shape that can match zero rows and report success); eight are provably safe — `scheduleGenerator`/`issueLink` bulk link expiry, where zero matches is the *correct* outcome; `handle_ripple_unsubscribe`, which reads the ripple row and returns `token_not_found` before updating; and `ripple_reminder`/`check_schedule`/`processAdherenceWithdrawal`/`StudySessionRunner`, which update rows they just selected. **The one real find: `CheckinFlow.saveIntention` recomputed `local_date` from the browser clock at intention-save time**, while the check-in row had been written earlier in the flow with its own date — so a check-in started at 23:58 and finished after midnight looked for tomorrow's row, matched nothing, and dropped the intention silently (the caller's `.catch()` only sees throws; a zero-row update isn't one). Fixed by threading the date `saveCheckin` actually wrote through its return value, plus `.select('id')` on the update so a zero-row result now logs a warning instead of passing as success. Deliberately **not** an upsert: that would mint a `ripple_checkins` row with an intention and no ratings, which would then count toward streaks and pollute the mood history. Also noted, not changed: ~40 of the 79 sites never inspect `error` at all, including all five `game_sessions` end-of-session writes and 10 of 11 `participant_schedule` writes — those rows do exist, so it isn't the same bug, but it is the condition that kept both of this week's failures invisible. Prior update: (**Ripple settings never saved for anyone without a `ripples` row — `update` matched zero rows and reported success** (2026-07-30, found by Norm on his own account): `/profile`'s five Ripple mutations (name, check-in toggle, cadence, reminder on/off, reminder time) each ran `.update({…}).eq('user_id', userId)`. PostgREST treats zero matched rows as success, and the page set local state optimistically regardless — so every control appeared to work and nothing was written, with the truth only visible after a reload. **180 of 186 profiles have no `ripples` row**, including Norm's, so this was close to universal for anyone who didn't create one through onboarding. The `disabled={!ripple}` guard that was meant to catch exactly this never fired, because the loader stores `{}` when there's no row and `{}` is truthy. Same silent no-op fixed in two more writers: `CheckinFlow`'s streak update (a row-less user's streak and `last_checkin_on` evaporated — which also kept them out of `ripple_reminder`'s query, since it selects from `ripples`) and `WelcomeFlow`'s Habit step (safe today because the NAME step upserts first, but it would have discarded a user's first reminder choice on any path that skipped it). All now `upsert` on `user_id` (`ripples_user_id_key`; every other column has a default or is nullable, so an insert carrying only the changed field is valid), and failures render an error instead of nothing. Verified by simulating the exact upsert under `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` with Norm's claims inside a rolled-back transaction: rows 0 → 1, `reminder_enabled=true`, `reminder_time=evening`, cadence defaulted `daily`, so RLS ("ripples: own rows", FOR ALL, `WITH CHECK user_id = auth.uid()`) permits the insert. **Rule: a Supabase `update` keyed on a user column is a no-op, not an error, when the row is absent — use `upsert` for anything a user can reach before the row exists.** Prior update: (**Field Guide: all ten personality disorders promoted to Tier A; tier labels now explain themselves** (2026-07-30): the taxonomy seed had carried a flag on the narcissistic-PD row since the day it was written — L11 teaches all ten PDs in full, so the tier split disagreed with the lecture, and a student who has just sat through a full lecture and then finds a 150-word stub concludes the wiki is thin. Norm took the upgrade: **Tier A 46 → 53, Tier B 52 → 45**, catalogue still 123 (pages move between tiers, none are added), fall scope now **78 generated pages at ~17 review hours** (was 71 / ~15.5). It also reorders `reference_worklist`, which sorts Tier A first, so those seven now rank above the remaining stubs for WP4. Separately, `tier A` meant nothing to anyone who hadn't read the taxonomy doc, including a TA — cards and page headers now read **"central to the course"** / **"supporting page"** from a shared `tiers.js` so the copy can't drift between the two surfaces. Two deliberate choices there: a **visible legend as well as hover text**, because `title` does nothing on a touch device and this is a wiki read on phones, so hover alone would have explained the labels to staff on laptops and nobody else; and the Tier B copy says *"shorter because of review time, not because it is off the syllabus"* — the tier is a review-budget device, so "nice to know" would tell a student they can skip material the exam covers. The label describes the page, never the importance of the disorder. §29a. Prior update: (**Caller-JWT verification decoupled from `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`** (2026-07-30): `send_message`, `create_participant`, `create_anonymous_participant` and `send-class-verification-email` each built a client from `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` purely to call `getUser()` on the caller's token. That var is deprecated in favour of publishable keys (the dashboard no longer shows it) and the legacy JWT pair it held was revoked this morning — when it stops being injected, all four lose their auth path with a 401 indistinguishable from an expired session. Each now verifies via `createClient(url, serviceKey).auth.getUser(token)`, with the role read on the same service client, which for a *gate* is what you want (true role, not the RLS-visible one). No `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` reference remains under `supabase/functions/`. **The first deploy was botched**: the new `const token` collided with an existing `token` later in the same scope in two of the four (the participant link token; the class verification token), so `create_anonymous_participant` and `send-class-verification-email` returned 503 BOOT_ERROR for ~7 minutes — only this session's probes hit them. The second was invisible to the smoke test because `verify_jwt: true` means the gateway answers before the function boots. And the first 503 was misdiagnosed as an esm.sh import failure and "fixed" with an unrelated import change *before reading the error*, which had said `Uncaught SyntaxError: Identifier 'token' has already been declared` the whole time. **Lesson: boot failures live in `get_logs service: edge-function-runtime`, not `edge-function` — a function that fails to boot never becomes an invocation, so the log you reach for first is empty.** Renamed to `callerToken`, import reverted, all four verified booting and returning clean 401s to no-auth and bogus-JWT probes (`send_message` v19, `create_participant` v5, `create_anonymous_participant` v13, `send-class-verification-email` v4). Prior update: (**Field Guide: the two duplicated pages merged; gap rule corrected once more** (2026-07-30): first real use of `edit_page()`. `major-depressive-disorder` went from three copies of the six-section skeleton to one, **15,825 → 11,032 chars**; `persistent-depressive-disorder` from two to one. Reading them mattered more than the mechanics: MDD's third copy already contained the first verbatim — the model's later pass had effectively integrated it, so the merge was mostly deletion — while PDD's *second* copy was genuinely additive, supplying the criteria structure (copy 1 described the category's history but never the symptom list) and the legacy DSM-IV prevalence and sex ratios, which closed a gap copy 1 had declared. "Keep the longest copy" would have lost real content. Wiki-wide, `wiki_links` went **45 → 71 with 0 red**, because the merges linked concepts the prose already named. Merging PDD then exposed a flaw in the morning's gap rule: "a gap is a section where no copy holds prose" silently lost the **partially filled** case, so a section with real content that still carries a `> **Needs research:**` marker read as complete — PDD came out reporting no gaps while its own body asked for research in three places, and `reference_worklist` would not have targeted any of them. Corrected in `20260730_wiki_needs_partial_sections.sql`: a gap is a declared marker **or** an empty section, which also matches what the prompt means by the marker (a *sourcing* gap, not a scientific controversy — those belong in Contested). Shadow-diffed against all 44 pages first: exactly one page changed. PDD's Epidemiology marker was narrowed rather than deleted, since onset-age and cross-cultural data really are still absent — a page that overstates its completeness is worse than one that admits a hole. §29a. Prior update: (**Field Guide: the wiki had no edit path** (2026-07-30): `edit_page(page_id, content, note)` — until now an accepted page could not be corrected by anyone. `review_proposal()` needs a *pending* version so it only ever accepts what an ingest proposed, `unpublish_page()` only hides a page, and `wiki_pages` has no authenticated write policies, so a typo on a page 300 students read required service-role SQL. Same one-audited-function shape as the other two write paths (SECURITY DEFINER + internal `is_course_staff()`), so there is still exactly one client-reachable way to change a body. Three choices worth keeping: **history is automatic** — the existing snapshot trigger records the previous body and the touch trigger bumps the version, so the function only labels the snapshot the trigger just wrote, and that recoverability is what lets the UI be a plain textarea rather than a ceremony; **the note is optional**, unlike unpublish's mandatory reason, because an edit leaves a diff and a forced field mostly collects the word "fix"; and **blanking is refused**, because a bodiless page is a *shell* awaiting its first proposal, making that a retirement (`unpublish_page`) not a correction. Verified in one rolled-back transaction under the instructor's JWT: blank/no-op/non-staff all refused, and a real edit bumped the version, kept the old body as an accepted snapshot, attached the note, extracted a new wikilink, and **re-derived the gap list — clearing `etiology` because the edit filled it**, which demonstrates the body-derived `needs` self-correcting on a live edit. Reader gains a staff-only **Edit page** button that re-fetches after saving instead of patching its own copy. Still not done: MDD and PDD themselves, which no longer misreport gaps but still read as three copies and two — merging them is editorial judgement, not mechanical. §29a, `20260730_wiki_edit_page.sql`. Prior update: (**Field Guide: the gap mechanism was lying, and a third proposal action** (2026-07-30): the WP2 reader was click-tested and works — which is how it earned its keep on day one, by making duplicated disorder skeletons visible (`major-depressive-disorder` carried the six H2 sections **three times**, `persistent-depressive-disorder` twice, one copy per accepted `update`). Two problems behind it, the smaller being the repetition. **`needs` was wrong, and `needs` aims WP4**: `extract_page_needs()` parsed the frontmatter `needs:` list while the merge pre-fill strips an addendum's frontmatter (correctly — two YAML blocks in one file is invalid), so the gap list froze at the *first* source's assessment. MDD declared 4 gaps and PDD 1, and all five were already filled further down the same page; since `reference_worklist` reads `needs`, the content sprint would have chased closed gaps and skipped new ones. Gaps now derive from the body — a section is a gap when no copy of it holds prose — which is self-correcting and also caught two gaps the model had written placeholders for but never declared. Built as a shadow function and diffed against all 44 live pages before swapping: 40 unchanged, the 4 that moved were exactly the corrections; backfill confirmed to create 0 version snapshots and leave `updated_at` alone. **Root cause: two prompt rules contradicted each other** — six H2 sections "ALWAYS" on disorder pages vs an update carrying "only the new information to merge" — so every update emitted a skeleton the pre-fill appended, and WP4's targeted reference runs would have reproduced it across all 46 Tier A pages. Paper mode now scopes the skeleton to `action: new`; **reference mode returns a complete page with the new `action: 'replace'`**, which overwrites rather than appends and is a distinct action precisely because the review UI must not pre-merge it. Still open: **there is no way to edit an accepted page at all** — no `edit_page` RPC, no authenticated write policies — so the two duplicated pages stay as they are and a typo is uncorrectable. Migration `20260730_wiki_body_needs_and_replace.sql`, §29a. Prior update: (**Six SECURITY DEFINER functions were reachable by anonymous callers — NULL is not false** (2026-07-29): found while gate-testing the new diagnostics RPC, whose `IF NOT is_super_admin() THEN RAISE 'forbidden'` did not fire for a caller with no identity. `is_super_admin()` was `SELECT COALESCE(super_admin, false) FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()` — with no JWT the query matches **no rows**, a SQL function returning no rows yields **NULL** (the inner COALESCE never runs), and `NOT NULL` is NULL, which is not TRUE, so execution fell straight through the guard. `my_role()` is NULL the same way, making `my_role() = 'lab' OR is_super_admin()` evaluate to NULL. Verified over real HTTP with only the public anon key that ships inside the client bundle: `admin_list_users` returned **200 with 184 rows including every email address**; `get_liliana_credit_report` returned participant rows with display names and credit hours. The same guard shape sat in `admin_set_user_role`, `admin_delete_user`, `duplicate_study` (not probed — they mutate) and in `get_class_participation` / `get_checkin_quiz_results` / `get_checkin_mood_results`, which expose class members' `utoronto_email` and a quiz answer key. All six fixed and re-probed as anon: refused (`20260729_null_guard_security_fixes.sql`). RLS policies are unaffected — a NULL policy expression filters the row out, so NULL fails closed there; it is only dangerous in `IF NOT …` control flow. radlab-academic swept and clean (`is_course_staff()`/`is_course_member()` are `select exists(…)` → false, and both write RPCs raise `no identity for caller` before any staff check). **Convention: a boolean helper used in `IF NOT …` must never be able to return NULL — wrap the SUBQUERY, not the column, and prefer `select exists(…)`.** Prior update: (**Diagnostics tab for scheduled services** (2026-07-29): `/admin/diagnostics`, super-admin only — `admin_service_diagnostics()` + `Diagnostics.jsx` (own 9.8 kB chunk), built after the Ripple 401 went unnoticed for 15 days. Ordered by how far each signal can be trusted, which pg_net's design dictates: credential shape is static and would have caught that bug on day one; `cron.job_run_details` is durable but records the *enqueue*, so a 401 logs `succeeded`; `net._http_response` carries the real status but has **no url column** (the queue row holding the url is deleted on completion) and pg_net prunes to ~31 rows / a few hours — so attribution goes by response-body shape via `diag_signatures()`, and a 401 body is unattributable, hence the separate unattributed non-2xx count. The durable canaries are the trustworthy part: `overdue_pending` for the email engine, `ever_reminded` for Ripple. The canary's first version read **48, not 0**, because it counted the permanent residue of withdrawn enrollments (pass 0c skips them forever; step 0b only sweeps `link_sent`/`unlocked`, never `pending`) — it now excludes withdrawn and reports them as `withdrawn_residue`. Live `prosrc` hashes identical to the migration file. Prior update: (**PSY240 email path configured end to end; two week-1 rate limits found** (2026-07-29): radlab-academic now sends through Resend (`smtp.resend.com:465`, key scoped to sending on `course.radlab.zone` only, so a leak of the credential in that dashboard field cannot send as `mail.radlab.zone`). Sender is deliberately **course-neutral** — `accounts@course.radlab.zone` / "RADlab Courses" — because Supabase allows one sender per *project* and this project hosts many courses; per-course identity belongs on the invite Edge Function, composed from `courses.code`. Three rate limits raised, all per hour: `rate_limit_email_sent` 2 → 300, `rate_limit_otp` 30 → 300, `rate_limit_verify` 30 → 300. Two findings worth keeping: **the email cap cannot be raised until custom SMTP exists** (Supabase pins it at 2/hour on its shared sender, which reads as a broken setting rather than a precondition), and **`rate_limit_otp`/`rate_limit_verify` are separate counters the email cap doesn't cover** — the week-1 QR path puts ~200 students through request-and-click inside one lecture, which would have failed after 30 of each as a generic error on their phones, and `rate_limit_verify` cannot be engineered around because every click verifies a token through Supabase auth however the mail was sent. That closes the last external dependency in WP5; the Ripple-onboarding collision is now its only open decision. Not yet exercised: an actual send — a correct config and a working one are different claims. §11. For a fork gate the estimate now simply **is** tomorrow, by assignment — the RPC runs at the moment of completion, so the materializer's `max(gate_completion_day + 1, today)` admits no other answer.
