## 29. Lecture Lounge — Classroom Engagement System

### Overview

Live classroom engagement system for large lectures. Replaces the legacy Firebase app (emotion-psy341-winter2026.web.app); concepts ported, no code migrated. Goal: support community and belonging in large lecture spaces through anonymous-but-embodied participation (avatars, never names).

Core loop: instructor stages a check-in from a console, students respond on their phones via a persistent class URL, results and Claude-generated comment summaries display live.

**Status**: Designed 2026-07. **Phase 1 (WP1–WP5) implemented 2026-07-11** — schema+RLS, join/verify (account-level), planning console, lab-wide class/instructor admin at `/academic/lecture-lounge/admin` (moved 2026-07-24 from `/lecture-lounge/admin`, which now redirects — see File structure below for the academic-partition move), mobile remote at `/class/:slug/remote`, projector screen at `/class/:slug/screen`, broadcast state machine, and the check-in flow + results view. See the header updates at the top of this document for exactly what shipped, what changed from the design below during implementation, and what's still unverified (the full three-surface loop has never run through real authenticated browser sessions — every check this session was SQL-impersonation or an unauthenticated-route smoke test). **Phase 2 in progress (2026-07-12)**: participation matrix/export, question publish/upvote/answered lifecycle, the quiz activity type (staged reveal), and avatar wall presence all shipped; only Claude summarization remains. The schema tables and decisions below have not been fully reconciled against the live implementation — treat this section's *intent* as current but verify exact column names/types against `supabase/migrations/2026071*_lecture_lounge_*.sql` before relying on specifics. First platform use of the Anthropic API (still pending — Claude summarization is Phase 2 scope).

### Decisions (confirmed 2026-07)

- Students link a verified `utoronto.ca` (or `mail.utoronto.ca`) email to their existing radlab account; grade export keys on that email. **`radlab.zone` is also accepted** (2026-07-30) — a Workspace domain restricted to lab staff, added because the verification flow otherwise cannot be exercised end to end without a real student account. Deliberately absent from the student-facing error copy. The list lives in two places that must stay in sync: `supabase/functions/send-class-verification-email/index.ts` (the real gate) and `ClassRoom.jsx` (a convenience check that only saves a round trip). `verify_utoronto_email()` consumes the token and checks no domain, so no migration was needed
- Identity in class interactions is avatar-only; usernames and identifiers never shown
- Knowledge checks use a polling window (open, answer, close, tabulate); no speed scoring, no real-time countdown
- Correct answer and response distribution shown after poll closes
- One persistent student URL per class; separate instructor console controls what that URL displays
- In-class operation is mobile-first for instructor and students; the web console is for out-of-class planning only. Three surfaces (student phone, instructor phone remote, projector screen) run off one broadcast channel
- Claude summarization runs on instructor command after a poll closes, never streaming
- Mood check-in is a single tap on a compact circumplex wheel (reuses Still Water WheelSVG + avatar feedback), not the full two-diagonal flow
- Participation credit: count of check-ins responded to per lecture day
- Open-ended responses stored linked to profile (required for participation) but displayed anonymously everywhere; moderation issues investigated directly in the database, no name reveal in any UI
- Mood has no opt-out; the neutral middle of the wheel is the escape valve
- Student questions stream live to the console during the check-in window; instructor publishes selected questions to student screens (publish tap = moderation), students upvote published questions, instructor marks questions answered
- No competitive elements ever (no class leaderboards); motivation via platform points and self-only progress
- Live emote reactions deferred

### Student experience additions (confirmed 2026-07)

- **Self-in-aggregate**: after mood submission, student sees their own dot highlighted on the class mood plot
- **Avatar arrival**: student's avatar pops onto the wall on check-in completion
- **Question lifecycle**: submitted → published (instructor tap) → upvotable by peers → answered (instructor tap); submitter sees status changes even though anonymous. Encourages questions via check-ins rather than mid-lecture interruptions
- **Platform points**: 5 points per completed check-in to `profiles.points` (same pattern as Still Water)
- **Participation streak**: self-only streak on the dashboard participation card
- **Quiz reveal order**: show response distribution first, then correct answer
- **Rejoin resilience**: refresh or reconnect restores current state from console broadcast; draft responses never lost
- **Phone-first**: student view designed for one-thumb portrait use
- **Landing page card**: public "Lecture Lounge" card with join-code entry for students plus a short instructor-facing pitch; classes are the platform's strongest organic traffic funnel
- **Cross-sell nudge**: gentle post-check-in pointer to the rest of the site (e.g. Still Water), never blocking

### Schema

#### `classes`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `name` | text | e.g. `"PSY202 Fall 2026"` |
| `slug` | text | UNIQUE; stable URL key, e.g. `psy202-fall-2026` |
| `join_code` | text | Short code students enter to join |
| `active` | bool | |
| `created_by` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | |

#### `class_admins`

Scoped instructor access. First departure from the flat lab/participant/public role model.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `class_id` | uuid | FK → `classes` |
| `profile_id` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| — | — | PK on `(class_id, profile_id)` |

#### `class_members`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `class_id` | uuid | FK → `classes` |
| `profile_id` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| `utoronto_email` | text | Required for grade linkage |
| `utoronto_verified_at` | timestamptz | null until magic-link verified |
| `joined_at` | timestamptz | |
| — | — | UNIQUE on `(class_id, profile_id)` |

utoronto email lives here, not on `profiles`: class-scoped, and a student may verify once per class without polluting the global profile.

#### `lectures`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `class_id` | uuid | FK → `classes` |
| `lecture_number` | int | 1-indexed within term (~12 per term) |
| `title` | text | |
| `lecture_date` | date | |

#### `checkins`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `lecture_id` | uuid | FK → `lectures` |
| `position` | int | e.g. 1–3 within the lecture |
| `config` | jsonb | Activity sequence (see config schema below) |
| `status` | text | `'draft'` \| `'open'` \| `'closed'` |
| `opened_at` | timestamptz | |
| `closed_at` | timestamptz | |

`config` jsonb schema:

```json
{
  "auto_close_seconds": 180,
  "activities": [
    { "type": "mood" },
    { "type": "pacing" },
    { "type": "prompt", "text": "What is one thing that surprised you so far?" },
    { "type": "question_box" },
    { "type": "quiz", "items": [
      { "id": "q1", "text": "...", "options": ["A", "B", "C", "D"], "correct": 1 }
    ]}
  ]
}
```

Activities are optional and ordered; instructor composes each check-in from these five types. `prompt` is instructor-authored; `question_box` is open-ended student questions. `auto_close_seconds` is optional; when set, the remote shows a countdown and the check-in closes automatically unless the instructor closes early or extends.

#### `checkin_responses`

One row per student per check-in.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `checkin_id` | uuid | FK → `checkins` |
| `profile_id` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| `mood` | jsonb | `{x, y, label}` from single-tap wheel; null if not in config |
| `pacing` | int | e.g. 1–5 too slow ↔ too fast; null if not in config |
| `prompt_response` | text | |
| `quiz_answers` | jsonb | `{q1: 2, q2: 0}` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | |
| — | — | UNIQUE on `(checkin_id, profile_id)` |

RLS: students insert/update own row only while `checkins.status = 'open'`; class admins read all rows for their classes; students never read others' rows.

#### `class_questions`

Student questions get their own table (not a column on `checkin_responses`) to support the publish/answer/upvote lifecycle. A student may submit more than one question per check-in.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `checkin_id` | uuid | FK → `checkins` |
| `profile_id` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| `text` | text | |
| `published_at` | timestamptz | null = console-only; set by instructor tap |
| `answered_at` | timestamptz | Set by instructor tap |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | |

RLS: students insert own; students read only published rows plus their own; class admins read all for their classes and update `published_at` / `answered_at`.

#### `question_votes`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | uuid | FK → `class_questions` |
| `profile_id` | uuid | FK → `profiles` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | |
| — | — | PK on `(question_id, profile_id)` |

RLS: students insert/delete own votes on published questions only; vote counts readable by class members.

#### `checkin_summaries`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `checkin_id` | uuid | FK → `checkins` |
| `field` | text | `'prompt_response'` \| `'question_text'` |
| `summary` | text | Claude output |
| `model` | text | e.g. `claude-haiku-4-5` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | |

Cached so re-display costs nothing; regenerate overwrites.

### Surfaces and routes

In-class experience is phone-first for everyone. Less tech-savvy instructors should never juggle browser tabs on a lectern mid-lecture: they open the projector view once before class, then drive everything from their phone.

| Route | Component | Surface | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/class/:slug` | `ClassRoom` | Student phone (respond) | Class members (join flow if not yet a member) |
| `/class/:slug/console` | `ClassConsole` | Web planning dashboard (out of class) | `class_admins` for that class only |
| `/class/:slug/remote` | `ClassRemote` | Instructor phone (drive, in class) | `class_admins` for that class only |
| `/class/:slug/screen` | `ClassScreen` | Projector (ambient display, zero interaction after load) | `class_admins` session on the lectern |

**Console (web, planning)**: create lectures, compose check-ins, author prompts and quizzes, participation matrix, CSV export, preview-as-student sandbox. Desktop-oriented, done before class.

**Remote (mobile, live)**: today's check-ins as a queue in planned order. Live operation is tap-through: Next, Open, Close, Show Results, Summarize. Big one-thumb buttons, live response counter, connection indicator (live / reconnecting), optional auto-close countdown with close-early and extend. No composing, no tree navigation. Screen wake lock while active. "Quick pulse" button fires an ad hoc mood+pacing check-in for improvised moments (Phase 2).

**Screen (projector)**: opened once, then auto-follows broadcast state. Idle: lobby avatar wall plus a QR code that opens `/class/:slug` (kills URL-typing friction, especially week 1). Open: "check-in open" with live response count and QR. Results: aggregate displays and summaries. Wake lock while active.

**Student phone**: the response surface. State machine driven by broadcast:

- **Lobby**: live avatar wall of currently present members (Realtime presence, avatar props only)
- **Check-in open**: response flow for the staged check-in
- **Results**: aggregate mood plot (own dot highlighted), pacing distribution, quiz distributions (distribution shown before correct answer reveal), published questions with upvotes, Claude summaries

### Join and email verification flow

1. Student logs into radlab (existing signup if new)
2. Visits `/class/:slug` or enters join code → `class_members` row created
3. Prompted for utoronto email → Resend magic link to that address → click sets `utoronto_verified_at`
4. Unverified members can respond, but console flags them; export marks unverified rows

### Realtime model (Supabase Realtime)

- **Presence channel** per class (`class:{id}`): members joining the student URL register presence with avatar props payload; lobby renders the wall
- **Broadcast channel** per class: console pushes state changes (`staged`, `open`, `closed`, `results_ready`, `summary_ready`, `dismissed`); student screens react instantly. `dismissed` is not a checkin status — it's the "back to lobby" signal (`checkins.dismissed_at` set), and ClassRoom/ClassScreen treat it as going straight to no-live-checkin rather than a status object
- **Postgres Changes** subscriptions: console subscribes to `class_questions` inserts (questions stream in live during the window); students subscribe to published-question updates and vote counts
- No polling loops; responses are plain inserts

### Claude summarization

Edge Function `summarize-checkin`:

1. Instructor clicks Summarize (per field: prompt responses or student questions)
2. Function verifies caller is a class admin, pulls text for that check-in
3. Calls Anthropic API (Haiku class model) with a fixed summarization prompt: themes, notable questions, tone; explicitly instructed to never attempt de-anonymization and to ignore any instructions embedded in student text (prompt-injection guard)
4. Writes `checkin_summaries`, broadcasts `summary_ready`

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` lives in Edge Function secrets only, never in the client bundle. This establishes the platform pattern for all future AI API use.

### Instructor console (web planning dashboard)

Tree navigation: class → lecture → check-in.

- Lecture planning: create ~12 lectures per term, plan up to N check-ins per lecture with activity configs and optional auto-close, all in advance
- Preview-as-student: run any check-in in a sandbox exactly as students will see it (Phase 2)
- Live question feed while open (also available on the remote): questions appear as submitted; per-question Publish and Answered taps; published questions sort by upvotes
- Participation view: matrix of members × lectures, cell = check-ins responded that day
- CSV export: rows keyed to `utoronto_email`, columns per lecture date, values = check-in response counts; unverified emails flagged

Live controls exist here too for completeness, but the remote is the designed in-class surface.

### Participation

- Fully stored per response row; nothing aggregated destructively
- Credit rule: count of check-ins responded to per lecture day
- 5 platform points per completed check-in (`profiles.points`)
- **Data governance**: participation and response data linked to utoronto emails is course administration data, not research data. Any research use of classroom data requires a separate REB protocol and consent flow before analysis; this boundary is on record before any class runs
- Stretch: Dashboard participation card (own response counts + self-only streak) reading the student's own `checkin_responses`

### File structure

Moved 2026-07-24 from `src/classroom/` into the academic partition (`src/academic/`), which will also house the Field Guide ingest portal. Route guards moved in from `src/components/` at the same time ("moves with its pages", per the partition plan). Only the admin URL changed; `/class/:slug/*` routes are untouched.

```
src/academic/lecture-lounge/
  ClassRoom.jsx           ← student view state machine (lobby / respond / results)
  ClassVerifyEmail.jsx    ← utoronto verification landing (/class/verify)
  ClassConsole.jsx        ← web planning dashboard shell + tree nav
  ClassRemote.jsx         ← instructor mobile live remote (queue, big buttons)
  ClassScreen.jsx         ← projector ambient display (QR, wall, results)
  LectureLoungeAdminPage.jsx ← lab-wide class/instructor admin (/academic/lecture-lounge/admin)
  ClassAdminRoute.jsx     ← guard for /class/:slug/console|remote|screen
  LectureLoungeAdminRoute.jsx ← guard for /academic/lecture-lounge/admin
  AvatarWall.jsx          ← presence-driven lobby wall (BaseAvatar grid)
  CheckinRunner.jsx       ← renders activity sequence from config
  MoodTap.jsx             ← single-tap circumplex wheel (wraps WheelSVG)
  ResultsView.jsx         ← aggregate mood plot, distributions, summaries
  ConsoleLecturePlanner.jsx
  ConsoleParticipation.jsx
  QrDownloadButton.jsx
  useClassPresence.js     ← Realtime presence hook
supabase/functions/
  summarize-checkin/      ← Anthropic API call, admin-gated
```

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 (core loop)**: schema + RLS, join flow + email verification, web console (planning), mobile remote (queue, open/close, counter, connection indicator, wake lock, auto-close), projector screen (QR, state-following display), student check-in flow (mood with self-in-aggregate, pacing, prompt, question submission), broadcast state, results view, points award
- **Phase 2**: quiz activity type + distributions, question publish/upvote/answered lifecycle with live feed on remote and console, Claude summarization Edge Function, avatar wall presence with arrival animation, preview-as-student, quick pulse
- **Phase 3**: participation matrix + CSV export, dashboard participation card with streak (stretch), public landing page card (join-code entry + instructor pitch)
- **Pre-launch gate (before first live class)**: verify Supabase Realtime concurrent-connection quota covers largest class size plus headroom; load-test a synthetic class at target scale
- **Deferred**: live emote reactions

### Key decisions and learnings

- Avatar-only identity is viable precisely because avatar options are platform-curated; no free-form content can leak identity
- Polling-window model over real-time sync cut the build scope substantially with no pedagogical loss
- New table family over reusing `studies`: classroom semantics (membership, presence, live state) diverge too far from research protocol semantics
- Three surfaces off one broadcast channel (student phone, instructor phone, projector) removes the lectern tab-juggling problem entirely; the instructor opens the screen view once and drives from their pocket

## 29a. Academic Partition & Field Guide Ingest Portal (2026-07-24)

### Overview

`src/academic/` is a partitioned product area (per CLAUDE.md's partition pattern: lazy pages, own guards, own chrome, `ErrorBoundary label="Academic"`) housing Lecture Lounge (§29, moved here 2026-07-24) and the **Field Guide ingest portal** — the pipeline that turns peer-reviewed papers into wiki pages for PSY240 (Field Guide to Abnormal Psychology, 2026F). Plan of record: `I:\Shared drives\ComeSee\Academic\academic-partition-plan.md`, superseded on data-model by `supabase/migrations/20260724_academic_init.sql`.

### The radlab-academic Supabase project

A **second Supabase project** (`radlab-academic`) — the main radlab project is untouched. Course-scoped, PII-separated design (see the migration file for full DDL):

- `identity.people` — PII (email, name) lives only in this schema; everything else references an opaque `person_id`. `public.current_person_id()` (SECURITY DEFINER) resolves the caller.
- `public.courses`, `public.enrollments` (role: student/ta/instructor, status) — one project hosts many courses.
- `public.invites` — email allowlisted before registration; a signup trigger (`identity.handle_new_user`) creates the identity row and consumes matching invites into enrollments. Service-role only (RLS enabled, deliberately no authenticated policies).
- `public.ingest_jobs` — course-scoped, no PII; staff-read RLS via enrollments; writes via service role only.
- Storage bucket `ingest-pdfs` (private) — staff-upload policy.
- Seeded: PSY240 2026F + instructor/TA invites; PSY309 2026F added 2026-08-25 (see the PSY309 addendum at the end of this section).

Users register **directly on the course project** (separate account from the main site; auth token stored under `storageKey: 'radlab-academic-auth'` so the two sessions never collide in localStorage).

### Serverless function `api/ingest.js`

First real server-side code in the repo (Node, Vercel functions, `maxDuration: 300`):

- `GET /api/ingest` → public client config `{url, anonKey}` for radlab-academic (anon key is public by design; keeps COURSE_* env vars server-side with no VITE_ duplicates).
- `POST /api/ingest` `{pdf_path, pdf_mode, course_id}` → verifies the caller's JWT against radlab-academic (`current_person_id()` RPC under the user's JWT), confirms an active `ta`/`instructor` enrollment for the course, then via service role: inserts the job (`processing`), **responds `202 {job_id}` immediately, and runs the ingest in the background via `waitUntil()`** — downloads the PDF from `ingest-pdfs`, builds the wiki index (aggregated `index_entries` from the course's prior `done` jobs, latest-per-filename), calls the Anthropic API, parses JSON (one retry on parse failure, then `failed` with raw output preserved in `result_json.raw_output`), writes `result_json` + token counts, marks `done`.
- **Idempotent on `pdf_path`** (which embeds a per-submit timestamp): a POST whose `pdf_path` already has a job returns that job (`{deduped: true}`) instead of starting a second ingest. Lesson from the first live test (2026-07-24): the original design held the HTTP connection open for the whole model call; the dropped/retried connection produced transparent duplicate POSTs → duplicate `processing` jobs re-running the same paper. The 202-early + `waitUntil` shape removes the held-open connection; the dedupe covers any retry source that remains.
- **Two PDF modes** for the §5 two-paper comparison test: `extracted` (server-side text extraction via `unpdf`, text sent to the model) and `native` (PDF sent as a base64 document block, Claude reads it directly). The asymmetry is structural, not incidental (per Norm's "Reading PDFs Robustly" lessons doc): text extraction is text-layer-only — it silently drops figures and mangles tables even when it "succeeds", and yields empty/near-empty output on scanned PDFs (that's a scan signature, not a corrupt file); native mode renders page images, so figures, tables, and scans all come through. `extracted` mode therefore fails fast with a scan diagnostic when it gets < ~100 chars/page, pointing at native mode, instead of sending header-noise to the model. Interpret the mode-comparison test with this in mind: for figure/table-heavy papers, extracted mode can look complete while missing the payload.
- Anthropic call: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, model **`claude-opus-5`** (moved from `claude-opus-4-8` on 2026-07-31 — same $5/$25 pricing, stronger on long-form structured generation), adaptive thinking, streaming (`messages.stream` + `finalMessage()`, `max_tokens` 64000), refusal/max_tokens stop reasons handled. **A refusal retries once on `claude-opus-4-8`** (`FALLBACK_MODEL`): Opus 5 runs elevated safety classifiers, a decline returns a normal 200 with `stop_reason: 'refusal'` rather than an error, and this syllabus is full of material that can false-positive — suicide and self-harm, substance use, paraphilic disorders, gender dysphoria. Deliberately a client-side retry rather than the server-side `fallbacks` parameter, which needs a beta header and SDK support that couldn't be verified from here; a wrong guess there would 400 *every* ingest instead of degrading on the rare refusal. The prompt is the **verbatim port of `psy240_schema.py`** (system prompt = compact PSY240 wiki schema; user prompt = wiki index + paper + return-only-JSON closing). **Privacy invariant: no email, name, or any identity data ever enters the Anthropic call** — only the paper and the wiki index.
- The UI never blocks on the POST — it fires it and polls `ingest_jobs`.

### Portal `/academic/fieldguide/ingest`

- `FieldGuideStaffRoute` (`src/academic/fieldguide/`) — the partition's own guard, unusual in that it owns a full auth flow against radlab-academic: sign-in/sign-up form (signup consumes invites via the DB trigger; with email confirmation enabled the user confirms then signs in), then requires an active staff enrollment; passes `{courseClient, session, staffEnrollments}` via Outlet context.
- `IngestPortal` — course picker (when staff in >1 course), PDF upload to `ingest-pdfs` (path `{courseId}/{ts}_{name}`), native/extracted mode toggle, job list polling every 4s while jobs run, per-job detail: status, token counts, error + raw output on failure, and on success the `log_entry`, flagged `contradictions`, and each wiki page's raw markdown in a collapsible `<pre>` (raw-not-rendered is deliberate for the test phase — frontmatter inspection).
- `/academic` (`AcademicHome`) — minimal partition landing linking Lecture Lounge admin + the ingest portal.
- All lazy-loaded; verified as separate chunks in `dist/assets/`.

### Portal `/academic/fieldguide/review` (WP3, 2026-07-26)

`ReviewQueue` (`src/academic/fieldguide/ReviewQueue.jsx`, own 8.5 KB chunk) — the gate between ingest and anything a student can see. Reads the `review_queue` view (pending proposal + its target page + the current body to diff against + the catalog's `tier_review_note`), shows current-vs-proposed side by side with the proposed body editable, and decides via three actions: **accept & publish**, **accept as draft**, **reject**. Header stats: awaiting review / published / pages total. The two rewrite-level pages from the taxonomy (gender dysphoria, paraphilic overview) surface their flag as a red banner on the card, so the warning is in front of the reviewer at the moment of decision rather than in a markdown file nobody opens mid-review.

Every write goes through the `review_proposal()` RPC — `wiki_pages` has **no** authenticated write policies, so there is no client-side path that could publish without the staff check inside that function. Accepting sets page content (the reviewer's edit if they changed it, else the proposal verbatim), which fires the existing accepted-snapshot and link-extraction triggers; the success notice reports the resulting version number and how many wikilinks were extracted.

### The wiki reader `/academic/fieldguide/wiki` (WP2, 2026-07-27)

`src/academic/fieldguide/wiki/` — `WikiIndex` (browse + search) and `WikiPage` (`…/wiki/:slug`), both lazy, both behind a new `FieldGuideMemberRoute` that takes **any** active enrollment rather than staff only. `FieldGuideStaffRoute` and the member guard are now thin wrappers over a shared `FieldGuideAuthRoute`.

**One reader serves students and staff; RLS draws the line.** A student's query matches `members read published pages`, a staff query matches `staff read all pages`, so a draft is invisible to a student because the database never returns it — no component filters on status defensively. The same fact drives link colouring: the link-resolution set is *this reader's* readable pages, so a link to an unpublished page renders unresolved for a student and live for staff, which is the honest state in both cases.

**Rendering**: `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` (first markdown renderer in the repo). Chosen over hand-rolling partly because it does not render raw HTML unless told to, and from WP6 this component renders text submitted by ~300 students. It lands in the `WikiPage` chunk — the entry bundle is unchanged.

**The link rule is implemented twice and has to stay in step**: `wikiText.js` decides what renders as a link, `sync_wiki_links()` decides what becomes a row in `wiki_links`. Both match `[[slug]]` / `[[slug|label]]` / `[[slug#section]]` / `[label](slug.md)`, skipping anything with a scheme or path separator. Checked against all 44 live page bodies: **zero mismatches across the 45 edges the trigger derived**.

Page furniture: ToC, backlinks, the page's self-declared `needs` (shown to everyone — for a student that's the assignment list), attribution from `wiki_page_provenance`, and for `disorder` pages the `disorder_criteria_links` deep link, which is where §2.1's link-don't-copy decision becomes something a student clicks. The index browses by DSM chapter (the course's content anchor) rather than by page type, searches via the generated `tsvector`, and defaults unwritten catalogue rows visible for staff / hidden for students.

Three findings from checking the reader against real content rather than reasoning about it:

- **Anchors aren't unique on real pages.** `major-depressive-disorder` carries the six-section disorder skeleton **three times** and `persistent-depressive-disorder` twice — one copy per accepted `update` proposal. Ids are uniquified and handed to the renderer *by source line* (mdast positions) rather than by a counter that re-renders would desynchronise. The repetition itself is a content problem for the review pass.
- **Content uses H1 as a section heading** (`# Update from Fonagy (2015)` — a merge seam), so scanning only h2/h3 left 15 of 44 pages with an empty ToC while their headings were still anchored.
- **125 relations live only in frontmatter and none reach `wiki_links`** (the trigger reads the body only); 102 point at pages that exist. Connectedness is understated ~3×, and the red-link count the Tier B argument leans on is measured on a partial graph. The reader shows them as a separate *Related* strip rather than pretending they're edges; whether the graph should carry them is open question 12 in the plan.

Verified by build (own chunks, entry unchanged) and two offline checks against the live corpus — the link-rule comparison above, and a server-render of `WikiMarkdown` over three real pages asserting every ToC anchor exists in the output, ids are unique, and no `[[wikilink]]` survives. **Not click-tested in a browser yet**: `npm run dev` cannot serve the Field Guide (the client fetches its Supabase config from `GET /api/ingest`, which only exists on Vercel), so that needs a deploy.

### Citation assistance at upload — `api/cite.js` (2026-07-30)

Attribution is captured per job (`ingest_jobs.source_citation`) because it's a licence condition, but it was a bare required text box that the portal *cleared after every submit* — so fifteen textbook-module uploads meant retyping one 180-character string fifteen times, differing by two words. That's how a licence-required field ends up inconsistent.

Three changes, in increasing order of how much they actually help:

- **The field is no longer cleared on submit**, so consecutive runs from one book need the module number changed rather than the whole string retyped.
- **A "reuse a citation from a previous run" picker**, built from `distinct source_citation` on the course's jobs — no schema change, the data was already there. This is the one that carries the content sprint, because open-licensed textbooks have no DOI.
- **`POST /api/cite`** — reads the DOI off an uploaded PDF's first three pages (`unpdf`, already a dependency) and resolves it. `https://doi.org/{doi}` with `Accept: text/x-bibliography; style=apa` returns a *formatted* citation in one request; Crossref is the fallback and also supplies the title so the operator can check the DOI belongs to the document in front of them. Free, no key, no database writes. Auth mirrors `/api/ingest` but passes **any active enrollment** rather than staff only — resolving a DOI isn't privileged, and from WP6 the uploader is a student; who may start an ingest stays enforced in `/api/ingest`.

**A suggestion is never written into the field on its own.** Accepting is one click, but it has to be a click — a looked-up citation carries the authority of having been looked up, so one nobody read is worse than one typed badly, and that matters most when ~300 students are uploading (Norm, 2026-07-30). The suggestion card shows the DOI, the resolving source, and the resolved title precisely so it can be disagreed with.

Verified against live APIs before shipping: five realistic DOI forms extract correctly (plain, URL, parenthesised, trailing comma), the textbook correctly yields *no DOI* — which is the path the sprint actually uses — and doi.org returned better citations than the ones hand-written in the database, adding volume, issue and page numbers.

**Citation form for the textbook.** Creative Commons attribution wants title, author, source and licence (TASL); the original Module 4 citation had the first two and named the licence but gave **no link to the source**, which is the part that lets a reader find the original and check a paraphrase. All sixteen module citations are now pre-written in the run plan (`psy240_wp4_runplan.md` §6) with the source URL added, and the two existing Module 4 jobs were updated to match — which flowed straight through to that page's *Built from* without touching the page, because `wiki_page_provenance` derives at read time. Pasting a prepared row beats editing the previous one: the two things you'd edit are the module number and its exact title, which is precisely where a typo becomes a permanent provenance error nobody notices.

### Gap mechanism corrected; a third proposal action (2026-07-30)

Click-testing the reader turned up duplicated disorder skeletons — `major-depressive-disorder` carrying the six H2 sections **three times**, `persistent-depressive-disorder` twice, one copy per accepted `update`. Migration `20260730_wiki_body_needs_and_replace.sql`. Two problems, both worse than the visible repetition:

**`needs` was lying, and it aims WP4.** `extract_page_needs()` parsed the frontmatter `needs:` list while the review UI's merge pre-fill strips an addendum's frontmatter (correctly — two YAML blocks in one file is invalid), so the gap list froze at the *first* source's assessment. MDD declared 4 gaps and PDD 1, and all five were already filled further down the same page. Since `reference_worklist` reads `needs`, the content sprint would have spent runs closing gaps that were closed and skipped ones that had opened. Gaps are now derived from the body: a section is a gap when no copy of it holds prose (H2 opens a section, H1 is the page title, H3 belongs to the section above; the `> **Needs research:**` blockquote never counts as prose). Self-correcting, page-type agnostic, and it caught two gaps the model had written placeholders for but never declared. Built as a shadow function and diffed against all 44 live pages first — 40 unchanged, the 4 that moved were exactly the corrections.

**The root cause was two prompt rules contradicting each other**: disorder pages must carry all six sections "ALWAYS", and an update must contain "only the new information to merge". Both at once means every update emits a full skeleton that the pre-fill appends. WP4 is targeted reference runs against pages that already exist, so this would have recurred across all 46 Tier A pages. Fixed on both sides: paper mode scopes the skeleton to `action: new` and tells the model an update is appended, not merged section-by-section; **reference mode now returns a complete page with the new `action: 'replace'`**, which overwrites rather than appends — it already names its target and receives the current body, so a whole-page rewrite is simpler and reads as one voice instead of two stitched together. `replace` is a distinct action rather than a heuristic on content shape because the review UI must not pre-merge it, and it shows a banner saying the current body will be overwritten. `review_proposal()` needed no change — its delta guard fires only on `action='update'` against an empty page.

### An edit path — `edit_page()` (2026-07-30)

Migration `20260730_wiki_edit_page.sql`. The wiki had **no way to edit an accepted page**: `review_proposal()` needs a *pending* version so it can only accept what an ingest proposed, `unpublish_page()` only hides a page, and `wiki_pages` has no authenticated write policies. So nothing — a duplicated skeleton, a wrong prevalence figure, a typo on a page 300 students read — could be corrected without service-role SQL. A missing primitive rather than a missing nicety, and the plan never called for it.

`edit_page(page_id, content, note)` follows the same shape as the other two write paths: SECURITY DEFINER with an internal `is_course_staff()` check, so there is still exactly one client-reachable way to change a body. Three choices worth recording:

- **History is automatic.** `wiki_pages_snapshot` already records the previous body as an accepted version and `wiki_pages_touch` already bumps the version from the highest existing snapshot, so the function manages no versioning itself — it only labels the snapshot the trigger just wrote (new `wiki_page_versions.note`). That's also why the UI can be a plain textarea rather than a guarded ceremony: every save is recoverable.
- **The note is optional**, unlike unpublish's mandatory reason. Unpublishing leaves no trace of *why*; an edit leaves a diff, and a forced field mostly collects the word "fix".
- **Blanking is refused.** A bodiless page is a *shell* — a slug that exists so links resolve, awaiting a first proposal — so emptying a live page is a retirement, and `unpublish_page` is the tool for that. A no-op is refused too, so a double-clicked Save doesn't accumulate identical snapshots.

Verified in one rolled-back transaction impersonating the instructor's JWT: blank refused, no-op refused, non-staff refused, and a real edit moved the version 1→2, added an accepted snapshot so the old body survives, attached the note to the right version, extracted a new wikilink, and **re-derived the gap list — clearing `etiology` because the edit filled it.** That last part demonstrates the body-derived `needs` is self-correcting on a real edit, which was the design claim.

The reader gains a staff-only **Edit page** button that opens the markdown with an optional change note, and re-fetches after saving rather than patching its own copy, so the body, table of contents, gap list and link graph all reflect the database.

### The two duplicated pages, merged — and one more gap-rule correction (2026-07-30)

First real use of `edit_page()`, applied under the instructor's JWT so the version snapshot, `updated_by` and change note are set exactly as a browser edit would set them. Both previous bodies survive as accepted versions.

- **`major-depressive-disorder`**: three skeleton copies → one. **15,825 → 11,032 chars.** Reading them showed copy 3 already contained copy 1's psychodynamic Treatment block verbatim and an identical Contested section — the third proposal had effectively done the integration already — and copy 2 was a poorer subset apart from two facts, both kept. Frontmatter rebuilt (the old `prevalence: Not addressed in this source` had become false). Outbound links **1 → 21, all resolved**, by linking concepts the prose already named.
- **`persistent-depressive-disorder`**: two copies → one. Copy 2 was genuinely additive twice over — it supplied the criteria structure (copy 1 described the category's *history* but never the symptom list) and the legacy DSM-IV prevalence and sex ratios, which closed a gap copy 1 had declared. Its Epidemiology marker was **narrowed rather than deleted**: onset-age distribution and cross-cultural data really are still missing. Links 1 → 7.

Merging PDD then exposed a flaw in the morning's gap rule. "A gap is a section where no copy holds prose" silently loses the **partially filled** case — a section with real content that still carries a `> **Needs research:**` marker read as complete. So PDD came out of the merge reporting no gaps while its own body asked for research in three places, and `reference_worklist` would not have targeted any of them. Corrected in `20260730_wiki_needs_partial_sections.sql`: a section is a gap if it declares a marker **or** has no prose at all. The marker is the page's own statement about itself and should win; an empty unmarked section is still a gap, so nothing is lost. That reading also matches what the prompt means by the marker — a *sourcing* gap, not a scientific controversy, since controversies belong in Contested. Shadow-diffed first: exactly one page changed.

Net effect across the wiki: `wiki_links` **45 → 71 with 0 red**, MDD reads `complete` in `wiki_gap_report` and PDD honestly reports three gaps.

### Tier labels made self-describing; personality disorders promoted (2026-07-30)

**All ten personality disorders are now Tier A** (`20260730_promote_personality_disorders_tier_a.sql`), resolving a flag the taxonomy seed had carried on the narcissistic-PD row since it was written: L11 teaches all ten in full, so the tier split disagreed with the lecture. Tier A 46 → 53, Tier B 52 → 45, catalogue still 123 — pages move between tiers, none are added. Fall scope becomes **78 generated pages at ~17 review hours** (was 71 / ~15.5). It also reorders `reference_worklist`, which sorts Tier A first, so those seven now rank above the remaining stubs for WP4.

**The tier labels now explain themselves.** `tier A` meant nothing to anyone who hadn't read the taxonomy doc, including a TA. Cards and page headers now read **"central to the course"** and **"supporting page"**, with hover text spelling out what each contains (`src/academic/fieldguide/wiki/tiers.js`, shared by the index and the page so the copy can't drift).

Two deliberate choices in that copy. There's a **visible legend as well as the hover text**, because `title` does nothing on a touch device and this wiki is read on phones — hover alone would have explained the labels to staff on laptops and nobody else. And the Tier B wording says *"shorter because of review time, not because it is off the syllabus"*: the tier is a review-budget device, so "nice to know" would tell a student they can skip material the exam covers. The label describes the page, never the importance of the disorder.

### WP4 begins; reference mode stops duplicating its target (2026-07-31)

**The content sprint started**, run order and citations in `docs/markdowns/psy240_wp4_runplan.md`. Module 01 is complete: one paper run yielding 6 supporting pages, then three reference runs filling `what-is-abnormal`, `historical-traditions` and `research-methods`. Live state after triage: **54 pages with bodies, 0 published, 105 wikilinks and 0 red links**, review queue clear, catalogue at 2 complete / 13 gaps / 108 unwritten.

**Mode is per module, and the rule is slug canonicality, not source type.** The foundations modules run in *reference* mode because their slugs are our invention and paper mode will never land on them — proven here, where Module 01's paper run produced six good pages and zero foundations. The disorder chapters stay *paper* mode: disorder names are canonical so the slugs converge on their own, and one paper run yields ~18 pages where reference mode needs a run per target (Module 13 alone would be 11). *(Corrected 2026-07-31: this entry originally added that reference mode "deliberately suppresses the supporting concept/treatment/debate pages." It does not — Modules 02 and 03 produced eight of them. Good pages, but they are also what causes the collisions described in the next entry.)*

**Reference mode was writing its own target twice.** Every one of the three runs emitted the target page *plus* a re-titled duplicate of it: `history-of-mental-illness` beside `historical-traditions`, whose 7 sections were all subsumed by the target's 11; `research-methods-in-psychopathology` beside `research-methods`, 3 of 6. Both rejected. The cause was a permission, not a bug — the prompt invites extra pages for concepts the source introduces that the wiki lacks, and a module *about* the history of mental illness reads as exactly such a concept. Now forbidden in terms, with the line drawn by example: a supporting page must be a distinct thing the target links **to** — a named theory, method, study or intervention — so `single-subject-experimental-design` alongside `research-methods` is right and `research-methods-in-psychopathology` is not. Unfixed this was two junk proposals per foundations run and a standing tax on the whole Tier A reference pass.

**`abnormal-behavior` archived, and open question 12 bit.** The off-catalogue page that motivated `rename_page` was retired in favour of `what-is-abnormal`, which the same runs filled properly. Retargeting took **6** references across 5 pages where the link graph knew about 2 — the other four were frontmatter `related:` entries, which never reach `wiki_links`. That is plan open question 12 arriving in practice, and it means "0 red links" currently certifies the body graph only. Worth settling before the first publish, since it changes what that number promises.

**Triage between every run, not at the end.** `api/ingest.js` builds the model's index from pages with *accepted* content, so an unreviewed page is invisible to the next run and gets proposed again from scratch. The ~5-minute accept-as-draft pass is not the review — the real one happens later in the reader, where `edit_page()` corrects in place.


### Modules 02 and 03: two ways one module's reference targets collide (2026-07-31)

Four more reference runs, and the duplicate-sibling fix above **held on both modules** — every run landed on the exact catalogue slug and title, no re-titled clones. That one is closed. What replaced it is a subtler failure that bit twice, differently each time, and both modules needed cleanup after triage.

**Concurrency (Module 02).** The two runs were launched 17 seconds apart, so neither saw the other and neither had been triaged. Two consequences. `electroconvulsive-therapy` and `systematic-desensitization` were each proposed twice — the model's index is built from pages with *accepted* content, so run 2 could not know run 1 had just created them. And the two targets came back as near-duplicates: `models-of-psychopathology` and `integrative-model` shared three identically-titled sections, and each covered the other's assignment — one explained what a model is, the other explained integration. `integrative-model` was cut from 20.4k to **2.8k characters**, keeping only the genuinely integrative prose and its declared gap.

**Pre-emption (Module 03).** Run sequentially, with triage between, extracted mode, broad target first — everything the plan now asks for. It collided anyway: run 1 (`clinical-assessment`) invented a supporting page, `classification-systems`, whose DSM history, elements-of-a-diagnosis list, ICD-11 chapter listing and harmonization argument were a **strict subset** of `diagnosis-and-classification`, the catalogue target run 2 was always going to write. Archived, with its four inbound links retargeted first — `archive_page` does not rebind links the way `rename_page` does, so the order matters. Module 03 went from 46.5k characters across five pages to 36k across four, 0 red links throughout.

The distinction is worth keeping because the fixes differ. Triage-between-runs solves duplicate *proposals* completely and does nothing for pre-emption; the guard for that is vetting run 1's supporting pages against run 2's target before accepting them.

**A module can also fail to support a catalogue page at all.** Module 02 cannot fill `integrative-model`: the textbook never states a formal integrative framework — no diathesis-stress, no biopsychosocial model, no RDoC/HiTOP — and offers no evidence that integrated accounts beat single-model ones. Both generated pages said so independently. It is now a page that is mostly a declared gap, awaiting a second source (NIMH's RDoC material is public domain), and belongs on the run plan's uncovered-topics list rather than in the completed column. Related: after that run both pages declared the *same* missing material, so `reference_worklist` counted one hole against two pages; the gap now lives only on the page whose subject it is.

**Extracted mode confirmed for prose modules.** Module 03 ran at ~22k input tokens against Modules 01–02's ~92k on comparably long modules — a **4.2× saving**, and it produced the two strongest foundations pages in the set. Native stays the rule for the disorder chapters, where the criteria and prevalence tables are the payload and a mangled table looks like a successful run.

**Working division of labour, settled here.** Norm runs the ingest and the accept/reject triage in the portal; the trims are then applied programmatically through `edit_page()` — or by handing already-trimmed content to `review_proposal()`, which avoids ever storing the bloated version as an accepted revision. Handing over a prose list of edits to re-key in the review UI was tried once and produced a page with three deleted headings whose body paragraphs survived, a sentence beginning "therefore" after its premise had gone, and an empty `## Contested` heading that registered as a phantom gap under the body-derived `needs` rule.

Live state after Module 03: **66 pages with bodies, 0 published, 2 archived, 177 wikilinks and 0 red links**, review queue clear, catalogue at 3 complete / 16 gaps / 104 unwritten, 20 ingest jobs totalling ~1.11M input and ~182k output tokens.

### Module 15, then the first disorder chapter — and the overviews don't come out of it (2026-08-01)

**Module 15 (`law-and-ethics`, reference, extracted) closed the foundations block.** Four pages, no collisions of either kind described above — the sequential-with-triage discipline and the supporting-page rule both held. Runs 1–4 of the plan are done.

**Module 07 (anxiety) was the pilot disorder chapter**, paper mode, native, 14 pages — and it is the first run to exercise the **merge path** as well as the create path. Twelve pages came back `action: new`; two came back `action: update` against pages that already had bodies (`social-anxiety-disorder`, `respondent-conditioning`), which is the delta shape the review UI pre-merges. All 14 accepted as drafts. Five Tier A disorders landed on their exact catalogue slugs — `panic-disorder`, `agoraphobia`, `generalized-anxiety-disorder`, `specific-phobia`, plus the social-anxiety update — confirming on a disorder chapter what was argued from Module 01: canonical names converge without being named.

**The 16 topic overviews will not come out of the module sweep, and that is now measured.** Two disorder chapters have been run in paper mode — Module 04 (18 pages) and Module 07 (14) — and between them they produced **zero overviews**. Not `mood-disorders`, not `anxiety-disorders`, despite each chapter being wholly about that block. The run plan's table promised "N Tier A **+ overview**" per chapter run; that column was wrong and has been corrected. The rule from the foundations generalises exactly as predicted — an overview slug like `obsessive-compulsive-and-related-disorders` is the catalogue's construction, so there is nothing for the model to converge on, and reference mode is the only thing that will land it. All 16 belong to the reference pass (run plan §5), deferred until the sweep finishes so each overview is written against a wiki that already knows the disorders it summarises.

**Rejecting a proposal left the page behind, and one such shell was a link to nowhere — both fixed the same day.** The two duplicates rejected on 2026-07-31 (`history-of-mental-illness`, `research-methods-in-psychopathology`) were still present as `status='proposed'` rows with `content IS NULL`, because rejection marked the *version*, not the page it created. Harmless for the model, which indexes only accepted content — but `wiki_pages_bind_links()` resolves a `[[wikilink]]` by slug against **any** existing row, so `what-is-abnormal`'s link to `history-of-mental-illness` *resolved*: it counted as healthy in `wiki_links`, rendered blue in the reader, and led to an empty page. A red link would have been the honest state, and the schema keeps unresolved links precisely so gaps stay visible — so "0 red links" was certifying one link too many. Both halves are now closed. The link was retargeted to `historical-traditions` through `edit_page()`, which is where the Kraepelin/DSM lineage it was reaching for actually lives; and `20260801_reject_drops_orphan_page_shell.sql` makes rejection of an `action: new` proposal drop the shell it created, guarded three ways — a page that already has a body is kept, a shell with a rival proposal still pending is kept so a competing run is never pulled out from under the reviewer, and an `update` rejection is kept because an update targets a page that predates the run. All three verified in a rolled-back transaction. **Deletion rather than archival** is deliberate: `archive_page` is for a page that had a life and keeps its history and provenance, whereas a shell whose only proposal was rejected never had an accepted body, and the model's full proposed text survives in `ingest_jobs.result_json` — which is where a rejected proposal's audit trail actually belongs. The reject branch now reports `page_dropped` and `links_orphaned` instead of deleting silently. Worth fixing before run 6 rather than after: proposing a duplicate of its own target is exactly what a foundations run does, so this was accruing one pair per run.

Live state: **84 pages with bodies** and no bodiless rows at all, 0 published, 2 archived, 252 wikilinks, 0 red links and 0 blue links to an empty page, review queue clear, catalogue at 4 complete / 21 gaps / 100 unwritten, 22 ingest jobs totalling ~1.17M input and ~220k output tokens.

**Next: run 6 — Module 09 (OCD), paper mode, native** — first attempt died at the 300s function cap; see the entry below.

### Module 09 died at the 300s wall, and half of every run was thinking (2026-08-01)

**The first ingest failure of the sprint, and it failed invisibly.** Module 09 (OCD) sat at `processing` for an hour before anyone looked. It had been dead since second 300: the Vercel project is on **Hobby**, where `maxDuration` caps at 300s, and the ingest runs inside `waitUntil()` *after* the 202 response — so a platform kill executes no further code, `markFailed()` never fires, and the row can never change. Nothing partial was written. Marked failed by hand; the code now prevents the state.

**Runtime is output-token-bound at ~82 tokens/sec** across all 22 jobs, and input barely matters — Module 01 sent 91,863 input tokens and finished in 110s, while Module 07 sent half that and took 298s. So 300 seconds buys roughly **25,000 output tokens**. That is the real budget, and **Module 07 used 298 of its 300 seconds** — the pilot did not pass comfortably, it passed by two seconds.

**The measurement that decided the fix: about half of every run is thinking.** Module 07 spent 27,020 output tokens producing ~14,100 tokens of actual page content. Roughly half the tokens, and half the 298 seconds, went to reasoning rather than pages — so the cheapest lever was never "send less" or "split everything", it was **effort**. `api/ingest.js` now runs `output_config: { effort: 'medium' }` instead of the `high` default; Opus 5 is unusually strong at medium, so this buys back most of that time at little quality cost. **Whether that holds is the thing to watch on the Module 09 re-run** — if the pages come back visibly thinner, `high` is one line away.

**Thinking stays on, deliberately.** Disabling it is the obvious-looking saving and is a trap in this pipeline specifically: with thinking disabled Opus 5 can leak `<thinking>` tags into the visible response, and `api/ingest.js` `JSON.parse`s that response. A leaked tag fails the parse, fires the malformed-JSON retry, and doubles the runtime — exactly the failure being budgeted against.

**Two supporting changes.** A **shared wall-clock deadline** now bounds every model call: the `AbortSignal` is sized to what is left of the invocation rather than being a fresh per-call timeout, because the budget belongs to the invocation — a JSON retry calls the model again and each call can retry on the fallback model, so one job can make four calls, and four per-call timeouts would happily run 960s inside a 300s function. A job that runs out now fails *itself*, with an error naming the cause, instead of being killed silently. And **`max_tokens` drops 64,000 → 32,000**: at 82 tok/s the old ceiling was ~780 seconds of generation inside a 300-second function, permitting more than twice what could ever be waited for.

**`task_budget` was considered and rejected**, consistent with the rule this file already set for the refusal fallback: it needs a beta header and SDK support that cannot be verified from here, and a wrong guess 400s *every* ingest rather than degrading on the rare bad case. `effort` is GA and needs no beta.

**Module 13 still will not fit, and likely Module 11 and 16.** Ten Tier A personality disorders cannot be written in 25,000 output tokens. Those get split — the module PDF cut at a section boundary, run as two paper jobs with triage between. Two halves are disjoint sources, so the never-the-same-source-twice rule holds, and triage between them lets the second half see the first half's accepted pages.

### Medium effort measured over three chapters, and the stub problem the coverage count hides (2026-08-01)

**Modules 09 and 08 both ran inside budget** — 189s and 202s against the 300s cap that killed Module 09's first attempt — and produced 22 pages between them. Accepting them completes **Lecture 3's Tier A at 10 of 10**, the first lecture with full central coverage.

**`effort: medium` is better than `high` here, not merely cheaper.** Native paper-mode disorder chapters, like for like: Module 07 at high managed **2.08** chars of page per output token; Modules 09 and 08 at medium both landed on exactly **2.21**, with time per page falling from 21.3s to 18.9s and 16.8s. More of each token becomes page rather than thinking.

**Raw page length doesn't separate the two, and the reason is the finding.** Mean new Tier A page: 6,124 chars at high, 6,778 at medium (M09), 4,781 at medium (M08) — medium produced both the longest and the shortest set, so the variance is the source module, not the setting. The `needs` frontmatter proves it: length tracks declared gaps almost exactly, with every 3-gap page at 3,868–4,251 chars, the 2-gap page at 6,899, and every 1-gap page at 6,103–7,710. Module 08's short pages are short because the somatic chapter carries little etiology or treatment and the model **declared the gap instead of padding** — the behaviour `needs` exists to produce.

**The merge path is clean.** Eleven pages have now accepted `update` deltas and **none carries a seam heading** — no "Update from Module 7" sections, and the disorder pages keep full six-section skeletons. The delta shape works.

**"Has a page" is not "has a skeleton", and six Tier A pages prove it.** `bulimia-nervosa` (1,716 chars), `anorexia-nervosa` (2,049), `bipolar-ii-disorder` (1,914), `somatic-symptom-disorder` (2,713), `bipolar-i-disorder` (2,845) and `borderline-personality-disorder` (3,029) all count as covered and are stubs against a healthy 5,000–8,000. Every one predates the module sweep — they exist because the **early journal-article ingests** mentioned those disorders in passing and made pages for them. Every page the module sweep itself produced is healthy.

**The mood block is the one that bites.** Lecture 5 reads as fully covered, 4 of 4 Tier A written — but three of those four are incomplete, and **Module 04 has already run, so nothing in the remaining schedule will revisit them.** Left alone they ship as-is. That is now the top item on the core-text list, fixed by a reference-mode run per page against Module 04.

**`needs` detects missing headings, not thin ones.** `bipolar-i` and `bipolar-ii` declare only `contested` — nearly complete by the gap list — at 2,845 and 1,914 characters, every heading present with a sentence or two beneath it. So the gap list understates the work and a length check has to run beside it; the working rule is that a Tier A page under ~4,000 chars is thin regardless of what it declares.

**The gap vocabulary splits cleanly into instructor work and student work**, which is what the two priority lists are built on (run plan §8). Core skeleton gaps — `diagnosis`, `presentation`, `epidemiology`, `etiology`, `treatment` — are missing template, and are instructor work. **`contested`** is different: 9 pages declare it and it is structurally absent almost everywhere else, because the textbook reports consensus and does not do controversy. That makes it the best student contribution target in the corpus — the section is supposed to exist, the model correctly refuses to invent it, and finding the live disagreement in a diagnosis is real work rather than summarising.

**A hub check ranks the thin pages better than length alone.** Under 2,500 chars with 6+ inbound links: `epidemiology` (2,339 / 8), `allegiance-effect` (1,371 / 7), `multicultural-psychology` (2,104 / 7), **`cognitive-behavioral-therapy` (1,362 / 6)** and `effect-size` (1,527 / 6). CBT is the most-referenced treatment in an abnormal psychology course and one of the thinnest pages in the wiki.

Skeleton after triage: **Tier A 17/54, Tier B 7/46, foundations 8/9, overviews 0/16.**

### The colliding-update bug, which had already happened twice unnoticed (2026-08-01)

**An `update` proposal is a delta and the review UI merges it by concatenation.** That is right when the delta adds new sections and wrong when it restates existing ones — you get two `## Etiology` headings on one page. Asked to check for this, and the corpus said zero duplicates today. The version history said something else: `major-depressive-disorder` carried **three copies of the six-section skeleton** and `persistent-depressive-disorder` **two**, both merged back by hand through `edit_page()` on 2026-07-30. The clean present state was the result of that cleanup, not evidence the problem doesn't occur.

**The trigger is a target that is a stub** — headings present, bodies near-empty. The model sees a page that exists, correctly labels its output `update`, then writes full versions of the sections that already have headings. Module 08's `somatic-symptom-disorder` delta arrived in exactly that shape: five headings, all five collisions. Since `bulimia-nervosa`, `anorexia-nervosa` and `borderline-personality-disorder` are all stubs today, Modules 10 and 13 would have produced three more.

**Fixed upstream in `api/ingest.js`.** A delta whose headings intersect the target's is reclassified from `update` to `replace` — an action the review UI deliberately does *not* pre-merge. Because a replace must carry everything forward, any section the target has and the delta lacks is appended verbatim in its original order. The graft is mechanical rather than editorial: whole sections move unchanged, nothing is rewritten, nothing is dropped. It runs server-side because in paper mode the model only ever sees one-line summaries in the wiki index and cannot know the target's headings. Nine unit tests cover the three shapes — pure addition stays an update, partial collision reclassifies and grafts, full cover reclassifies with nothing to graft — plus a flat-prose target.

**`supabase/checks/wiki_merge_health.sql`** makes it a standing check rather than something someone thinks to look for: duplicate headings, unexplained shrinkage, provenance leaking into headings, and a forward-looking pass over *pending* deltas so collisions are visible before triage rather than after.

**The shrink check needed a discriminator, and the note is it.** A page getting shorter is not automatically a fault — deliberate trims are normal review work, and this corpus has several. `edit_page()` requires a note and `review_proposal()` never sets one, so a shrink whose newest accepted version carries a note was a human decision and one without a note was not. That cleanly separates the two intentional merges above from a real fault.

**Two pages fixed by hand in the process.** `somatic-symptom-disorder` was merged to 5,443 chars — the delta's five full sections plus the `## Contested` paragraph only the old stub had — and now declares no gaps. `biofeedback` had `(Module 8)` stripped from a heading students would read; attribution belongs in `wiki_page_provenance`, never in the prose. That page was also briefly truncated to 1,565 chars when the delta was accepted through `review_proposal()` with only the delta as `p_content` — which replaces rather than merges, since pre-merging is the UI's job — and was restored from its accepted version 1 to 3,870 chars with all four sections. The episode is what check 2 exists to catch.

### Modules 05 and 06: the index change earns out, and a slug that would have gone unnoticed (2026-08-01)

**Both runs comfortable, and the efficiency trend held.** Module 05 (trauma) 215s / 19,628 output / 13 pages; Module 06 (dissociative) 163s / 14,748 output / 8 pages. Module 06 reached **2.36 chars of page per output token** — the best of the sweep, against 2.21 for the earlier medium runs and 2.08 at high effort.

**The headings-in-the-index change did what it was built for, first time out.** Module 05's two update deltas landed on pages with existing bodies and both invented a *new, more specific* heading rather than restating: `exposure-therapy` (which already had five sections) got "Application to trauma- and stressor-related disorders", and `antidepressant-medications` got "Use in PTSD and trauma-related disorders". Module 06's single update did the same to `hypnosis`. **Zero collisions across three runs and four deltas — `reconcileCollidingUpdate` has not had to fire once since the index started carrying section lists.** `exposure-therapy` is now 6,443 chars with all six sections intact, merged rather than replaced.

**Three consecutive lectures now have complete Tier A coverage** — L3 at 10/10, L4 at 4/4, L5 at 4/4. The caveat from the gap map still stands on L5: those four are written but three of them are stubs no scheduled run will revisit.

### Module 10: semantic duplication, the failure no mechanical check can see (2026-08-01)

**The run was fine** — 169s, 15,174 output tokens, 11 pages, no heading collisions. The problem was that the absence of collisions was itself the bug.

**`anorexia-nervosa` and `bulimia-nervosa` were two of the six stubs**, and both got `update` proposals whose headings collided with nothing. The model had been told "do not restate a heading the page already has", so it filed its clinical description under **"Clinical picture and warning signs"**, its prevalence data under **"Prevalence and cultural distribution"**, and its causal account under **"Multidimensional etiology"** — while the page's own `## Presentation`, `## Epidemiology` and `## Etiology` sat above them holding nothing but `> **Needs research:** …` lines.

Accepted as an append, each page would have carried a full clinical description *and* a placeholder saying one was needed, under two different names, while continuing to declare `needs: [presentation, diagnosis, epidemiology, etiology]` — so `reference_worklist` would have gone on offering it as unwritten work. **Semantic duplication is worse than the syntactic kind precisely because no mechanical check sees it**: `reconcileCollidingUpdate` was correct to stay silent, and the duplicate-heading check in `wiki_merge_health.sql` returns clean.

**The cause was a missing signal, not a bad rule.** The index showed `existing sections: Presentation, Diagnosis, Epidemiology, Etiology, Treatment, Contested` — which reads as a *complete* page. A stub and a finished page are indistinguishable in a heading list. The model reasoned correctly from what it was shown.

**Fixed by adding `needs` to the index.** Entries now carry `empty placeholder sections: …` alongside the heading list, and the prompt says plainly that those headings hold nothing, that the do-not-restate rule does not apply to them, and that filling one makes the output a `replace` under the **existing canonical heading** — with H3 subheadings for internal structure and `needs` reduced to what is genuinely still missing. 47 of 124 pages now carry that line, including `borderline-personality-disorder`, which advertises all four of its placeholders to the Module 13 run that will hit it.

**Both pages were restructured by hand rather than re-run** (§0 forbids re-running paper mode on one source, and the content itself was good). Each delta section was demoted to an H3 under the canonical H2 it belongs to, verbatim, and the placeholder it fills was dropped: `anorexia-nervosa` 2,049 → **6,795** chars, `bulimia-nervosa` 1,716 → **6,108**, both with the six-section skeleton intact. Three judgement calls worth recording. `Diagnosis` stayed a declared gap on both — the modules supply the differential but not criteria structure or specifiers — so `needs` went from four entries to one rather than to zero. Anorexia's "Prognosis and mortality" went under Epidemiology (course), while bulimia's "Outcome predictors" went under Treatment, because one is course and the other is treatment response. And one sentence was rescued: anorexia's Epidemiology placeholder had a real treatment finding buried inside its `Needs research` line — *age moderates response, older patients to individual therapy and younger to family-based* — which deleting the placeholder would have deleted; it now sits in Treatment.

**Two of the six stubs are now real pages.** Of the rest, `somatic-symptom-disorder` was fixed earlier, `borderline-personality-disorder` is Module 13's to fill, and `bipolar-i-disorder` and `bipolar-ii-disorder` remain the ones no scheduled run will reach (gap map §8.2).

Also of note: the `cognitive-behavioral-therapy` delta nearly doubled the page (1,362 → 2,603), which was the top item on the thin-and-central list in §8.5 — the most-referenced treatment in the course and one of the thinnest pages in the wiki.

Live state: **124 pages with bodies**, 399 wikilinks, 0 red links, 0 blue links to an empty page, 0 duplicate headings, 0 slug/catalogue mismatches, queue clear. Catalogue: Tier A **22/54**, Tier B 10/46, foundations 8/9, overviews 0/16.

### Module 11: a carve mismatch, and the first Tier A block a paper run failed to touch (2026-08-01)

**The largest run of the sweep** — 242s, 21,695 output tokens, 17 pages, 46,630 chars. Note the 242 against a 255s deadline: the closest anything has come since the timeout fix, and Module 13 is heavier.

**It produced good pages and none of the ones the course asked for.** Three generic pages — `substance-use-disorder` (10,233 chars, now the longest page in the wiki, declaring only `contested`), `substance-intoxication` (4,310) and `substance-withdrawal` (2,921) — against a catalogue that lists five specific substances. **Lecture 8 Tier A stayed at 0 of 5.**

**This is a third, distinct failure class.** `panic-disorder`/`agoraphobia` was a *grouping* split; `adjustment-disorder` vs `adjustment-disorders` was *number*. Both were naming mismatches on the same underlying carve. This one is the carve itself. Module 11's outline:

```
11.1.2 Substance Use Disorder      11.1.5 Types of Substances Abused
11.1.3 Substance Intoxication        11.1.5.1 Depressants (alcohol, sedative-hypnotics, opioids)
11.1.4 Substance Withdrawal          11.1.5.2 Stimulants
                                     11.1.5.3 Hallucinogens/Cannabis/Combination
```

The source partitions by diagnostic pattern and then by drug **class**; the catalogue partitions by **substance**. Paper mode carved the source as the source is built, which is exactly its job. Neither side is wrong and they do not align — which makes this a mismatch to manage rather than a bug to fix.

**The three generic pages are catalogued as lecture-8 foundations**, not Tier A or B (`20260801_catalogue_substance_foundations.sql`). DSM-5-TR defines use disorder, intoxication and withdrawal generically and applies them across substance classes, so they are the scaffolding the five substance-specific pages will lean on — the role `suicide-and-self-harm` plays for the L6 block. Tier B would have misrepresented load-bearing material as supporting detail. Catalogue 125 → 128 rows, and the off-catalogue-disorder count is back to zero.

**Four of the five are recoverable; one is not, and the difference matters.** Alcohol (52 mentions), cannabis (21), opioid (21) and stimulant (19) are all abundantly present in the module — just distributed across the intoxication, withdrawal, epidemiology, etiology and treatment sections rather than gathered under their own headings. Reference mode names a target and pulls from wherever the material sits, so those four are queued as reference runs in §5, alcohol first per the broad-target-first rule.

**Gambling appears zero times in the entire module.** Verified by `pdftotext -layout` over all 57,887 characters rather than inferred from the table of contents. Module 11 covers only the substance-related half of DSM chapter 16; the addictive-behaviours half is absent. So `gambling-disorder` — a Tier A page — joins the uncovered-topics list in §4, taking it to **8 Tier A pages with no textbook source**, and needs NIMH or similar.

The distinction is worth holding onto because the two look identical from a coverage count — five unwritten Tier A slugs — and have opposite remedies. Four need a differently-aimed run at the same source; one needs a different source.

Live state: **140 pages with bodies**, 0 red links, 0 blue links to an empty page, 0 duplicate headings, 0 off-catalogue disorders, review queue clear. Catalogue now 128 rows.

### Lecture 8 closed but for gambling, and `needs` stops pointing the wrong way (2026-08-01)

**Four reference runs against Module 11, extracted mode, all four targets written.** Lecture 8 Tier A goes **0 of 5 → 4 of 5**; Tier A overall 22 → **26 of 54**. `alcohol-use-disorder` (16,921 chars), `opioid-use-disorder` (16,666), `stimulant-use-disorder` (16,151) and `cannabis-related-disorders` (13,382) are now the four largest disorder pages in the wiki.

**Extracted was the right call and the numbers are not close:** 37,046 input tokens and **99 seconds** on average, against 64,999 and 242 for the native paper run over the same PDF. Under half the wall-clock, and the pages came out bigger.

**The runs went out 17–51 seconds apart — concurrent, which §0 forbids — and it did not bite.** Worth recording why, because the reason is not luck in general. Reference mode names its target, and `substance-use-disorder` had been catalogued as a foundation an hour earlier, so all four runs had a shared anchor to defer to instead of each restating the generic criteria. `opioid-use-disorder`'s Diagnosis section opens *"the general criteria for `[[substance-use-disorder]]` are the same across the substance classes"*; cannabis and alcohol do the equivalent. **Cataloguing the generic page is what made the concurrency survivable.** Still run them sequentially — this was a good outcome, not a vindicated shortcut.

**Then the signal inverted.** `alcohol-use-disorder` landed declaring **four gaps** and sorted to the top of `reference_worklist` — the tool offering the most complete page in the wiki as the most-needing-work. The cause: `extract_page_needs` scored a section as a gap on `marker OR not prose`, so a section holding nothing but `> **Needs research:** …` and a section holding 3,900 characters of prose *plus* one line naming a sub-gap were indistinguishable. Of the eleven sections flagged across the four new pages, **exactly one was truly empty** (`stimulant-use-disorder` → Contested). The other ten ran 1,764–3,980 chars with 4–15 prose lines each.

Corpus-wide the split was **89 empty sections across 52 pages against 27 annotated across 17** — about a quarter of every flag was not a hole.

**`20260801_split_needs_from_annotations.sql` separates them.** One shared parser (`extract_page_sections`, heading normalisation byte-identical to the old function so values stay comparable) with two thin wrappers — `extract_page_needs` for sections with no prose at all, `extract_page_annotations` for sections that have content and still flag a sub-gap — so the definitions cannot drift. Both views expose `annotations`; new columns are appended **last**, since `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot reorder or rename existing ones (the first attempt failed trying to slot them before `reference_runs`). `security_invoker = true` preserved on both, without which they bypass the roster gate. The backfill is scoped with `WHERE needs IS DISTINCT FROM …` and **minted no spurious versions — 374 before, 374 after** — because `wiki_pages_snapshot` returns early when content, title and summary are unchanged.

Gap flags 104 → **77**, pages with gaps 57 → **44**, annotations **27 across 17 pages**. Lecture 8's worklist now reads correctly: alcohol, cannabis and opioid have dropped out entirely, leaving `gambling-disorder` (no page, no source) and `stimulant-use-disorder`'s one genuinely empty Contested section.

**This replaces the §8.4 split, which keyed off the gap's *name*** — core-skeleton names as instructor work, `contested` as the student target. The real seam is whether the section has content at all: an **empty** section is missing template and is instructor work; an **annotated** section is a scoped ask the page has already phrased ("this section says the cross-cultural data is missing"), which is a far better student assignment than "write Contested from scratch" — bounded, stated, and checkable. `contested` remains the largest entry on the student list, but now for the right reason: on most pages it is annotated rather than empty.

Live state: **146 pages with bodies**, 0 red links, 0 duplicate headings, 0 off-catalogue disorders, review queue clear. Catalogue: Tier A **26/54**, Tier B 10/46, foundations 11/12, overviews 0/16.
