# Part IV — Operations

## 29b. Come, See prototype sketchbook (`public/prototypes/`, 2026-08-02→03, extended 2026-08-11)

Six self-contained prototype experiences for the Come, See sense-foraging platform — the receptive dynamics from the design compendium (`I:\Shared drives\ComeSee\come-see-design-compendium_Aug1_2026.md`, §4) that had never been built, each breaking one link of the task-mode verb chain see → want → act → get. The first five were built, agent-playtested, and merged in a single day (2026-08-02); **Sidelong** followed on 2026-08-11. Live at `/prototypes/` (index) as **inert static files** — plain HTML+canvas, no React, no Supabase, no auth, zero app-bundle impact.

| File | Dynamic | The verb | Grasping degrades how |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thaw.html` | Receiving impressions | Rub a fogged window; a winter garden lives beneath | Fast rubbing smears; hurry fogs the pane from below |
| `milkweed.html` | Letting go | Pop pods, carry seeds, release into the wind | Held seeds wilt; touching fliers knocks them down |
| `reply.html` | Call and quiet response | Offer a soft call (pitch = screen Y), then listen | Crowded/loud calling hushes the valley (capped, recovers) |

| `alongside.html` | Follow without catching | Walk beside a wisp at its pace | Approach dissolves it to mist (reforms within sight) |
| `stone.html` | Hosting | Be a stone; press-hold *attends* visitors | Taps ripple; visitors lift and circle back |
| `sidelong.html` | Averted vision | Rest the gaze; faint stars bloom *beside* it | Pointing at a faint star puts it out; darting empties the sky |

**Reply's register economy (2026-08-03, Norm's direction).** Each of the six creature types has a `PERSONA` entry fixing three things at once: a **home** index on the pentatonic ladder, a constellation **motion** (thrush flicks, owl breathes, frog pulses in unison, bellbug shimmers, whistler drifts in slow orbits, dove sways in pairs), and an idle **chirp** cadence. `home` is simultaneously the register a voice answers in — a reply takes the *contour* of the player's phrase and transposes it home, verified: the phrase `[2,4,3]` returns as 220/262/220 from the frog and 523/659/659 from the bellbug — and the band of calls that courts it (`near = 1 − |pitch − home|/5`). The eight voices people every rung 0–7 (repeated types are nudged off their kin). Trusted voices then **chirp on their own**, each at its persona cadence, gated on the valley not being hushed. The emergent result, measured: courting only the low end yields ~10 chirps per 90 s from 2 low types; courting the whole ladder yields ~19 from 4 types spread across it. **The night fills in proportion to how much of the register range the player has courted** — accumulation the player hears rather than a score, and the pitch-locality is what keeps it from saturating early (the earlier flat-mid-session problem).

**Alongside's two cellos (2026-08-03, Norm's direction — the previous audio was aversive).** The original layer had three genuinely unpleasant sources: a 4.1 kHz sine *gated by an 11 Hz square wave* (a piercing tone chopped eleven times a second, always on), a "bond pad" of two sines 0.5 Hz apart (a low drone beating slowly, swelling exactly as the player travelled with the wisp), and a high-passed noise burst on every dissolve. All three are gone. The wisp and the traveller are now each a faint bowed string — sawtooth pair through a resonant lowpass plus a body filter, bow noise, and vibrato — rooted on D3, and **distance is intonation**: out toward the band edges the player's string sits a sour fifth (−67 cents) and beats against the wisp's; through the middle of the companion band, at a shared pace, it glides true and the beating stops (measured: 0 cents together, −67.1 apart, 0 again on rejoining). Losing the wisp drops you to your own voice, out of tune and alone; the meadow bloom forces resolution and the ending chord was retuned to D major to land on the cellos' D and A. Three design points worth keeping: the **settling assist** (a smoothstep means reaching ~0.8 attunement completes the last of the distance for you — you come near and it arrives), **dissonance also recedes in volume** so being unattuned whispers rather than grates and consonance is never a loudness reward, and **pace-matching reads smoothed speeds inside a broad distance plateau**, because someone walking alongside is always correcting — an instantaneous-velocity test made the true fifth unreachable even for a perfect companion, which is what the first two tuning passes got wrong.

**Art pipeline (started 2026-08-03).** `docs/markdowns/alongside_asset_list.md` inventories all 16 drawn elements in Alongside — counts, pixel sizes, colours, anchors, motion — plus the three constraints an artist needs: the projection is **mixed 3/4 top-down** (uprights bottom-centre anchored, flats pre-squashed ellipses at 0.6), bodies must stay dark and neutral because the code animates glow separately (baking glow in would break "sites light when visited together"), and authoring is at 2× since DPR caps there and world units are 1:1 with CSS pixels. First art landed the same day: Norm's `grasspack.svg` (4 tuft variants) is **inlined as Path2D path data rather than loaded as a file** — the prototypes are single self-contained HTML files with no fetches or build step, and the source happened to contain four concatenated `<svg>` roots, which is not a loadable document anyway. Because each blade is its own path, blades sway with independent phase and outer blades trail; a rigidly rotated tuft sprite would have lost the ripple, which is the game's main "you are moving through a real place" cue.

**Sidelong — averted vision (2026-08-11).** The sixth dynamic, and the compendium's own first entry (§4.1, "the anti-Delve"). Promoted from a guided-meditation sketch (`f:\wideeye.html`) that had the right intent and none of the physics: a timed script of instructions over an animation nothing could touch, which by the compendium's test is a waiting room, not a foraging ground. Rebuilt so the dynamic is literal — **the pointer stands in for the gaze, and faint stars are only ever visible beside it**, which is true of the real eye, where rod density peaks well off the fovea. Look straight at a faint star and it goes out; that is the physics, not a penalty. Gaze stability is the global driver, per the compendium: sustained darting closes the whole field. The moon is the anchor — the one bright, easy thing to rest on, with its own extinguished blind spot around it. The **settling assist** is present (rest near the moon and the last of the opening completes itself) and the smoothed-speed lesson from Alongside is reused verbatim, since someone holding still is always correcting.

The retrospective gift is the inversion: a constellation that links itself out of stars found sidelong becomes **readable by looking straight at it** — the one act that until then put stars out — and gives up its name. Nothing announces this; playtests found players stumbling into it by sweeping across a linked figure. This is the interdependence loop (§6) in its cheapest possible form, and it is what the second half of the session is made of.

**What the agent playtest loop caught here** (the pattern from 2026-08-02, run again): (1) the **settling assist banked** — an uncapped pool of settled seconds kept the field pinned wide open for a minute after leaving the moon, so the global driver did nothing at all and a darting player still had a full sky; (2) the **band was wider than the screen** — with the falloff bottoming out at 1150 px, every pixel of a 1384 px viewport sat inside the findable zone and one minute of parking found 762 of 940 stars; (3) after fixing both, the content still **ran dry at t=151s of a 270s arc**, the same failure Milkweed had at ~2.5 min. That third one is why the sky is now larger than the screen and turns at 5°/min (the compendium's world-drift) with figures authored outside the initial view so they rise — and why the naming layer exists at all. Verified numerically rather than by eye: the visibility-by-distance profile reads 0.00 in the fovea, 0.97 through the 180–270 px band and 0.10 far out; direct fixation takes a star from 1.00 to 0.004 and letting go returns it; sustained darting takes the field to 0.05 and the visible faint count to zero while the sky stays a sky. Every behavioural profile reaches an ending, including a player who **never touches anything** (gaze parked on the moon, 8 figures still link as the sky turns past it) — and that player still does worse than one who moves, so travelling is rewarded without being required. Cost: sim 0.13 ms/frame at 1694 stars, render ~12.4 ms — the whole budget is fill rate across four full-screen passes, not star count, so DPR is clamped to 1.75.

**The soft-gaze pair (2026-08-15, Norm's prompt: "experiment with these effects as a game").** Two more prototypes from the perception-science families adjacent to Sidelong's averted vision, each a genuinely different receptive verb. **Soften** (`soften.html`) is the defocus/hybrid-image family (Oliva & Schyns, pointillism, the designer's squint test): a dusk valley whose ridge, cloudbank, hedgerow and meadow-shadow are also figures — but only at low spatial frequency. Press-and-hold softens the gaze (a slow ~1.9 s ramp; release snaps sharp in 0.4 s), implemented as a crossfade between two bakes of the same scene: one with all its high-frequency detail (drawn deliberately *across* the figure boundaries, because detail crossing an edge is what breaks a gestalt), and one that is **nothing but a blur of the first** — every pixel of the reveal derives from pixels already on screen, so softening only ever removes. The figures sit in the sharp bake at full, final strength, hidden by gestalt camouflage (their masses *are* ridge, cloud, hedge, shadow) plus a film-grain HF mask that averages to nothing under the blur. (The first build drew the masses faint in the sharp bake and re-drew them boosted onto the soft one, which made the reveal an overlay arriving rather than a thing that was there all along — Norm caught it on feel, 2026-08-15, and the emphasis pass was removed.) **Arbitrary images as hidden figures (same day, Norm's ask)**: any image from any source — an AI generator, a photo — can become a hidden figure via `__soften.embedImage(src, opts)` or, in `?dev` mode, by dragging an image onto the page. The insight that makes this trivial: *a low-frequency image is just a tiny image* — downsampled to 48 px its high frequencies are gone by construction, so smoothly upscaled, edge-feathered, and imprinted into the sky with a luminosity blend (form arrives in the sky's own hue) it hides under the same detail and grain as the authored figures, honesty preserved. The embedded figure registers in the settle physics like the others (default name "the visitor"). Verified end-to-end with the lotus-brain hero image: hides as cirrus, assembles under softness, settles as found. Generation itself stays external by design — prompt any generator for a *soft-edged single-tone silhouette on a flat background* (form survives the downsample; texture does not) and drop the result in; illusion-conditioned diffusion (ControlNet-style) that generates the whole camouflage scene is the known next tier if wanted. Scanning while holding breaks the squint (smoothed-speed strain, the Alongside lesson a third time). Two honesties anchor it: scotopic vision is genuinely low-acuity, so nightfall raises a softness floor for everyone — the zero-input player still gets the night's own staggered reveal of every unfound figure — and a found figure stays found even under the sharpest gaze, which is true of real hybrid images. The heron exists only in stars after dark: Sidelong's sky, seen from this valley. **Wallflower** (`wallflower.html`) is the peripheral-drift/Troxler family (Rotating Snakes, the scintillating grid): eight petal-ring dancers spin and travel *only while unwatched* — fixation stops them dead, visibly (dim + tuck), and they resume when released. Company courts them: near but not looked at, they accrue trust, come nearer, and at full trust each **blooms**, stamping a permanent flower into a never-cleared trail layer — the inversion made literal, since the trails and flowers hold still and reward direct gaze with everything the dance drew while unwatched. Chasing is a whole-field event (hush: everyone retreats and stills). The finale gathers all eight into a ring that stamps one last shared figure, and deliberately cannot be stalled by staring at it.

**What the playtest loop caught in the pair** (same method, run again): Soften shipped clean apart from art fixes (cloud scallops floating in empty sky; hedge scribble too sparse to camouflage the hare). Wallflower had two real ones. (1) A **death spiral**: trust pulled a dancer's orbit *inside* the watched band, where proximity to a merely-resting gaze read as being stared at — trust drained, the dancer froze, and frozen meant unable to leave; fixed by keeping the trust orbit outside the soft-watch radius, softening the drain, and giving a stared-at dancer a slow shy retreat so nothing can be pinned. (2) **The Sidelong parking failure, wearing flowers**: a gaze parked anywhere courted the entire clearing at once and bloomed all eight dancers by mid-session, beating every active player; fixed by proximity-weighting trust and courting only the three nearest companions. Verified gradient after: chase-and-stare profile 1 bloom, zero-input 4 by mid-session and 7 by the end (ending still reached), deliberate companion 5 by t=238. Perf: both under 0.3 ms/frame sim+render headless.

**Key decisions**

- Diegetic-only feedback everywhere: no meters, scores, counts, or accuracy; state renders as world (embers, fireflies, blooms, moss). One placeholder intro line each; tuning panel gated behind `?dev`/`t`.
- Non-contingent worlds: every prototype's events run without the player (wind pops pods, the valley calls first, visitors arrive, savoring sites self-stir) — the §2 "gifts must be non-contingent" principle, verified by zero-input playtest runs.
- **Headless-testable by construction**: each exposes `window.__<name>` with `skipTo(sec)`, a synchronous virtual-clock `step(n)`, and synthetic input driven through the real input path. This enabled the build→agent-playtest→fix loop that defined the day (see below). Sim state accrues from `dt`, never wall clock.
- Timeline arcs ~4.5–5 min ending in a "world completes it" gift (cold clears the pane; a finale gust; a nocturne + stranger voice; meadow bloom; a firefly that stays), with endings reachable for every behavioral profile including the silent/greedy/chaotic player — several fix passes existed precisely to guarantee this.

**The agent playtest loop (keep this pattern).** Each prototype was played headlessly by a subagent against the compendium's §2 safeguard checklist plus a "would a bored phone user stay 3 minutes" bar, measuring physics numerically before critiquing. They found what taste missed: Thaw's fog regrowth was silently dead (per-frame alpha below the canvas's 1/255 quantization floor) and its ending stalled at 90%; Reply's racket was uncapped (20 s of tapping bricked 4+ min) and silent players got no ending; Milkweed exhausted its content at ~2.5 min and desktop *hover* disturbed seeds; Alongside's mist-reform teleported the creature out of view for exactly the naive players most likely to chase it, and one approach to the settled wisp permanently broke the finale; Stone's night was a dead screen and its attend verb was inert for half the cast. All fixed and re-verified same-day; a final visual-QA agent swept all six pages (zero broken visuals, zero console errors). Browser-pane playtest mechanics (rAF throttling, `file://` refusal in scripted tabs, fronting via `tabs_select` to revive rendering) are recorded in auto-memory `reference_headless_canvas_playtesting`.

**Status**: merged to `main` 2026-08-03. All copy is placeholder pending Norm's voice pass. Open design threads: whether temporal contingencies (Reply's 6-s spacing, Stone's calm-before-minnows) need observation-line scaffolding — to be answered empirically from the debug APIs' behavioral signatures rather than assumed.

**Free Breathing (2026-08-21→24, `/dev/free-breath` — React route, not a static file).** The sketchbook's first *self-paced* breath experience: no pacer. Hold I/↑ (or an on-screen amber button) for the inhale, O/↓ (blue) for the exhale; hold nothing and the face waits — the face is First Contact's `ContactAvatar` unmodified, driven through an inverse-sine `getPhase` adapter that maps key-driven fullness onto its paced-cycle contract, with an outer scale wrapper so the growth reads unmistakably. Every hold/release logs a phase segment; Finish parses the log into per-breath `{inh, hold, exh, rest}` durations and draws each breath as a four-vertex shape — inhale up, hold right, exhale down, rest left; vertex distance rather than side length, because a side-length quadrilateral cannot close whenever one phase outlasts the other three combined, which a relaxed long exhale routinely does — overlaid with the point-wise session average and per-breath small multiples on one shared time scale. Parser normalization (2026-08-22, Norm's direction): a raise under 300 ms between two holds of the same phase fuses into the hold (accidental key-up, counts as breathing), and an in/out hold under 300 ms demotes to pause, so rapid flicker mints no breaths — the face still answers every press, since animation reads the live control state, not the parser. Tap coaching + an eight-breath target (2026-08-24): a sub-300 ms tap raises 'hold down the button for the whole inhalation/exhalation', and sessions carry eight progress dots with Finish available from the first complete breath. `src/games/FreeBreath/` (parser under node:test via `npm test`); unauthenticated, writes nothing; card on the `/prototypes` hub. Known next tier: propagate the session-average shape forward as a personalized pacer.

## 29c. The Workbench — sharing Claude Code sessions with lab members (2026-08-11)

Lab members get a page showing the Claude Code sessions Norm has explicitly shared with them, updating **while the work is happening**. Built from the handoff brief at `I:/Shared drives/ComeSee/ClaudePacks/radlab-session-sharing-handoff.md`; the brief's proposed data model was replaced in two places, both noted below.

**Routes**: `/workbench` (member view) · `/workbench/:sessionId` · `/workbench/admin` (Norm's console) · `/workbench/admin/:sessionId`
**Files**: `src/workbench/` (`WorkbenchRoute.jsx`, `WorkbenchAdminRoute.jsx`, `WorkbenchPage.jsx`, `WorkbenchAdminPage.jsx`, `SessionTranscript.jsx`) · `api/session-push.js` · `scripts/claude-session-push.mjs` · `.claude/settings.json` · `supabase/migrations/20260811_workbench_sessions.sql`

**Discoverability (2026-08-11)**: both routes are linked from the `/admin` sidebar, which is where lab members already are — `Workbench` in the last unheadered group (with `end` on the `NavLink`, so it does not also highlight on the admin path), and `Workbench admin` in the super-admin block. That block now renders under a hairline rule (`S.divider`, drawn from `section.divider`) so the super-only tier reads as a separate tier rather than three more entries on the same list. The links are UX only; `/workbench/admin` is still gated by `WorkbenchAdminRoute` and by `is_super_admin()` in RLS.

### The three decisions that shape everything else

**1. Tool output is never collected.** What travels is Norm's prompts, Claude's prose, and a one-line *headline* per tool call (`Edit src/App.jsx`, `Bash: run the build`). Not file contents, not query results, not diffs, not thinking blocks. This was Norm's call over a richer scrubbed feed, and it is the reason the feature is safe to run at all: sessions in this repo routinely hold participant rows, Supabase internals and shared-drive paths, and a scrubber has to be right *every* time whereas not collecting the data is right by construction. The endpoint still re-applies a secret scrub, because the realistic remaining exposure is a key pasted into a *prompt*.

**2. `role = 'lab'` is not a gate here.** It already grants `/admin/*`, so **every student in the lab holds it** — gating the Workbench on it would have shown all captured sessions to all of them while looking like access control. `claude_session_shares` / `claude_project_shares` are the entire access story; `WorkbenchRoute` checks only "are you signed in", and a member with nothing shared sees an empty shelf, which is the correct outcome and needs no guard. The console is **super-admin-only** — sharing decides who reads Norm's actual work, so it is his alone.

**3. Capture is per session and off by default — revised 2026-08-11 after Norm caught it.** The first design captured every session in a hooked repo automatically and relied on the share step to control who could *see* it. Norm's objection landed: that is continuous background recording of all his work in the repo, and *"nobody can see it yet"* is not the same promise as *"it was never recorded"* — only the second is worth making about someone's own working notes. So capture now requires an explicit per-session opt-in and `workbench.json` says only **where** and **how** to push, never **whether**. The cost is the one the original design was avoiding: a session nobody opted in is gone, and cannot be shared later. Norm took that trade knowingly.

### Departures from the handoff brief

- **No `lab_members` table.** The brief proposed one; lab members already exist as `profiles.role = 'lab'` with real logins, and a parallel roster would have been a second source of truth to keep in sync with `src/data/people.js` and with `auth.users`.
- **Turns, not a content blob.** The brief proposed `session_content(session_id, content, version)`. Append-only rows on `(session_id, seq)` instead: live updates become cheap inserts rather than rewriting a growing blob, a re-push after a lost high-water mark is a no-op instead of a duplicate, and history is kept for free — nothing overwrites a published turn.

### The turn-granularity bug, caught before anything was wired up

The distiller first merged consecutive assistant messages into one turn, which read better in the abstract. Run against a real 4-hour session (the Sidelong prototype, ~150 messages, ~200 tool calls) it produced **two turns**: one prompt, one enormous reply. Worse, that merged turn keeps `seq = 1` forever while its content grows — and the push path only sends turns above the server's high-water mark, so **a long session would have published one stale fragment and then gone silent for hours**, which is the exact failure the feature exists to prevent.

One turn per *message* is append-only and therefore stable: a turn, once written to the transcript, never changes. Grouping runs of assistant turns back into one readable block is `SessionTranscript.jsx`'s job, where it costs nothing and breaks nothing. Same component renders the member view and the console preview, so "preview" means preview.

### Pipeline

`Stop` hook (fires each turn) + `SessionEnd` hook → `scripts/claude-session-push.mjs` reads the session's JSONL transcript, distils it, and POSTs turns above its local high-water mark to `/api/session-push` → service-role upsert with `ignoreDuplicates`, so a re-push is a no-op. Member pages poll every 10s (not Realtime: a stale socket on a tab left open for three days costs more than an indexed query).

The hook **never fails the session** — every path exits 0. A sharing feature that can break Norm's actual work is worse than no sharing feature.

**Three independent gates, all must pass.** (1) The repo carries the hook registration in a checked-in `.claude/settings.json` — opt-in per repo rather than global, because the 28 project directories on this machine include MRI data, participant papers and the Handbook. (2) `~/.claude/workbench.json` exists, giving endpoint, token and a project allowlist matched by **path boundary** so worktrees under an allowed repo count and report under the parent's `project_key` — a standing project rule that silently skipped worktree sessions would read as broken. (3) **The session itself has been opted in**, via `node scripts/workbench-share.mjs on <session-id>` (`off`, `status` too). Norm's route is to say "share this session" and have Claude run it — *Claude: your own session id is the UUID in your scratchpad path, which matches your transcript filename; do not infer it from the newest file in the project directory, because concurrent sessions make that the wrong answer.* Opting in publishes the session **from its start**, not from the moment of opt-in. `off` stops further pushes but does not unpublish — deleting is a console action. Failing any gate → the script exits 0 silently, which is what makes the checked-in registration safe for anyone else who clones the repo.

### Verified 2026-08-11

Visibility proved live under `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` against three real accounts — see the migrations manifest for the full table. The load-bearing result: **with the session shared to Jaafar, sandy (also `role='lab'`) saw 0 sessions and 0 turns**, a member cannot read `claude_session_shares` to learn who else holds a session, and a member inserting their own share row is blocked with SQLSTATE 42501. Build clean; `WorkbenchPage`, `WorkbenchAdminPage` and `SessionTranscript` each emit their own chunk.

**Not yet verified**: nothing has travelled through `api/session-push.js` end to end — the endpoint needs `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` and `WORKBENCH_PUSH_TOKEN` set in Vercel, and the seeded session in the DB was inserted directly. The first real push is the outstanding test.

## 30. Key Learnings

- Safari/iOS: avoid `@keyframes` with custom properties inside SVGs, `foreignObject`, inline `<style>` in SVG groups. Move animations to document `<head>`. Use `setAttribute` + `requestAnimationFrame` for all SVG animation.
- Logo: use `RADlab_Logo.svg` (white outline) or `RADlab_Logo_light.svg` (dark outline) — never redraw. White outline sits directly on the pink nav background. Dark outline for any other light surface.
- `useRef`-based timing is the correct React pattern for RT measurement and breath timing. Never use `useState` for values read inside animation loops or timeouts.
- SVG attribute names in `setAttribute` must be hyphenated (`stop-color`, `stroke-width`, `flood-color`) — camelCase only works in CSS, not XML attributes. Gradients silently fall back to black if this is wrong.
- QUEST+ adaptive staircase (jsQuestPlus) for threshold tasks; SDT analysis for go/no-go (Pond Watch).
- **jsQuestPlus serialization**: save `normalized_posteriors` (not `pdfAll`, not `priors`) and `trial_count` per staircase. Restore by passing `saved.normalized_posteriors` as the `priors` argument to the new jsQuestPlus constructor — this seeds the new instance from the previous session's posterior. jsQuestPlus does not reconstruct `stim_list` on restore (so `stim_list.length` will be 0), but the posterior is correctly restored and `getStimParams()` will return the right next stimulus. Track `trial_count` separately in a `useRef` since jsQuestPlus doesn't restore it.
- **jsQuestPlus initialization timing**: the staircase hook must wait for the Supabase profile fetch to resolve before deciding whether to restore or initialize fresh. Use a `useEffect` that watches `savedState` and guards on `undefined` (still loading) vs `null` (confirmed no state). Initializing on mount before the fetch completes always produces fresh staircases regardless of saved data.
- **jsQuestPlus internal property**: trial count is `stim_list?.length` not `trialCount` — check the actual object shape rather than assuming property names.
- **Trials table schema**: always include `game_name` (indexed text column) and `cumulative_trial_number` (managed by a `BEFORE INSERT` Postgres trigger — never set from application code). Add `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()` for reliable ordering. The cumulative trigger queries `MAX(cumulative_trial_number)` across all trials joined to the same user via `game_sessions`, increments by 1, and sets it on the new row automatically.
- **Diagnosing staircase bugs**: if all staircases show identical posteriors after trials, check (1) whether `update()` is being called with the right response index (0/1/2 — never undefined), (2) whether the staircase key lookup is resolving correctly for all four conditions, (3) whether the `update()` call wraps the stimulus in an array (`staircase.update([log10Mag], responseIndex)`). A posterior identical to the prior after N trials means `update()` either wasn't called or received symmetric inputs that cancelled out.
- **New routes must be `React.lazy()`-loaded, never a static top-level import** (see CLAUDE.md's "Route code-splitting convention") — a static import in `App.jsx` pulls that whole page into the entry bundle every visitor downloads on every route. Discovered 2026-07-11 after zero code-splitting anywhere let the entry bundle grow to ~782 KB gzipped unnoticed.
- Supabase handles auth + DB — no custom backend needed.
- Windows PowerShell: no `&&` — run commands one at a time.
- For file updates: present individual changed files rather than repacking the full tarball.
- Avatar reset before each trial (including warmup start) must be synchronous: cancel `requestAnimationFrame`, call `resetAvatarToNeutral()` via direct `setAttribute` calls, then hold 1000ms via `useRef` timer before restarting the rAF loop. Any state-driven or `useEffect`-driven reset will be too slow — one or more frames will render before the reset takes effect.
- **jsQuestPlus psychometric function**: `getStimParams()` returns a plain scalar. `update()` takes a plain scalar too — `update(log10Mag, responseIndex)`, NOT `update([log10Mag], responseIndex)`. Wrapping in array causes NaN posterior silently.
- **jsQuestPlus Weibull P(correct)**: do NOT use `jsQuestPlus.weibull()` — that function returns P(incorrect). Implement P(correct) directly: `(1 - lapse) * (guess + (1 - guess) * (1 - Math.exp(-Math.pow(10, slope * (stim - threshold))))) + lapse * guess`. No `/20` divisor — slope 5.70 is already in the correct units for this parameterisation.
- **jsQuestPlus `psych_samples` order** must match the psychometric function's argument order exactly: `[thresholdSamples, slopeSamples, guessSamples, lapseSamples]`.
- **npm package name**: `jsquest-plus` (hyphenated) — not `jsquestplus`. Import as `import jsQuestPlus from 'jsquest-plus'`.
- **First Contact rolling buffer**: use a fixed-size 4-cycle buffer (`slice(-4)`) for sync scoring. Never use a cumulative mean — early poor cycles would permanently lower the score and make the 80% threshold unreachable.
- **Aura rings in SVG**: render ring circles *before* the head ellipse in SVG draw order so they appear behind the avatar, not on top of it.
- Platform theme is **awareness and attunement**, not water specifically. Game names should evoke noticing and change (Pond Watch, Ebb & Flow, First Contact, Deeper Contact) — contemplative and sensory rather than clinical.
- **React Compiler wiring on Vite 8 / `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6 — the obvious config is a silent no-op**: `react({ babel: { plugins: ['babel-plugin-react-compiler'] } })` (the standard Vite 7 method) builds green while compiling *nothing* — the Rolldown-based plugin-react no longer runs Babel, and there is no warning. Verify with an unminified build: `grep -c 'react/compiler-runtime' dist/assets/*.js` — 0 means the compiler never ran. The working wiring is `npm i -D babel-plugin-react-compiler @rolldown/plugin-babel`, then in `vite.config.js`: `import react, { reactCompilerPreset } from '@vitejs/plugin-react'`, `import babel from '@rolldown/plugin-babel'`, `plugins: [react(), babel({ presets: [reactCompilerPreset()] })]`. Measured on main@`c964dea` (2026-08-01): 556 functions compiled / 120 non-fatal bailouts, build 4s → 33s, total JS 1,137 → 1,308 KB gzip. Evaluated and deliberately **not** adopted — see the 2026-08-01 Last-updated entry and the Housekeeping roadmap item for the reasoning.
